content_zh: 因此,我为主而遭俘虏,求你按照你们被召唤的礼仪而行走。 (第4:1页) 这些话很重 他们的体重不是因为保罗从安静的书房或舒适的地方写作,而是因为他从监狱牢房里写作。 保罗不会像世界所定义的那样, 他在写作时, 对他的批评者来说,他是一个麻烦制造者. 一个危险的煽动者。 对上帝来说,他是一个忠实的仆人。 这很重要。 他敦促以弗所的教会记住并活下来。 他的话很重,因为他的生活支持他们。 他并没有要求他们做他自己没有做的事, 保罗的惊人之处是:他没有失败的可能。 他将前往地底, 宣扬基督, 将他关起来,他将成为“主的俘虏”,将他的痛苦变成福音价值的活生生的见证。 处决他? 精细。 正如他在别处所说的那样,“对我来说,是基督,而死亡是利益”(Phil. 1:21,ESV)。 保罗说,“福音已经不够了。 ” 他没有一刻可以得出结论,“这不值得。 ” 相反,保罗的整个生活,特别是他的痛苦,证明了这一真理:无论你的情况如何,相信福音永远不会白白浪费。 保罗并未入狱, 他入狱是因为他认为这个消息值得忍受. 这是一个重要的区别。 如果信息不值得痛苦, 基督教不会保证没有痛苦的生活。 它所许诺的是更好的事情:没有意义的痛苦。 希望苦难得不到最终结果。 这就是为什么保罗可以在两个科林斯语中说:“由于这种短暂的灾难,我们准备了一种永恒的光荣之分,超越一切的比喻,因为我们不看所见的事物,而看所见的事物。 所见之物是短暂的,而所见之物是永恒的。” 福音为我们提供了一个忍受暂时痛苦的框架,因为它将我们置于永久的承诺中。 现在我们可以忍受苦难, 我们的疼痛有结束期 为什么? 因为耶稣已经在我们的位置上遭受了完全的痛苦。 他自受其害、死亡、判决。他从坟墓中走出, 因为他,连死亡都无法战胜我们 当保罗敦促信徒们“以值得召唤的方式行走”时, 他邀请他们过着充满希望的生活, 这篇文章首次刊登在委员会的双周通讯《激进》上, 今日订阅.

title: Five Ways to Pray for Persecuted Christians
summary: Jamie Dean offers a prayer guide for persecuted Christians in Iran, China, North Korea, and other hard to reach nations.
summary_zh: 杰米·迪恩（ Jamie Dean ）为伊朗、中国、朝鲜和其他难以抵达的国家的受迫害基督徒提供了祈祷指南。
title_zh: 为受迫害的基督徒祈祷的五种方式
content: Sunday, Nov. 1, marks the annual International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church. It’s a day for believers across the globe to unite in concentrated prayer for Christians suffering for the gospel. Here are a few biblically-based ways to pray for the persecuted, along with a guide to a few specific nations to remember. 1. PRAY FOR THOSE IN PRISON “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them.” Hebrews 13:3 Iran : In 2025, Christians were sentenced to a combined total of more than 280 years in prison . Pray for those still in jail, and for families enduring separation. China : The Chinese government has continued its crackdown on believers, including several still in prison after a raid on Zion Church last year . Pray for gospel hope and perseverance. Eritrea : As many as 350 believers remained in jails in 2025, including some who have been imprisoned for decades . Pray for endurance and deliverance. 2. PRAY FOR BOLDNESS “And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness.” Acts 4: 29 Syria, Pakistan , Libya , Sudan : Danger and threats are a common experience for believers in these nations. Pray for the Lord to protect churches and give them boldness to proclaim Christ, even when it’s difficult. 3. PRAY THAT PEOPLE WILL COME TO KNOW JESUS “I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel.” Philippians 1:12 Afghanistan : In a country where it’s more dangerous than ever to follow Jesus, Afghans are still coming to know him. Pray believers will continue to be a witness, and that unbelievers will find true life in Christ. 4. PRAY FOR GOD’S BLESSING TO THOSE SUFFERING “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven…Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.” Matthews 5:10,12 North Korea, Somalia, Yemen: These are among the most difficult places in the world to follow Christ. Pray for the Lord to bless these believers facing severe persecution, and to strengthen them with the hope of heaven. 5. PRAY FOR THE PERSECUTORS “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.” Matthew 5:44 Nigeria: Christians in northern Nigeria have endured kidnappings and violence for years. Pray the Lord will stop their attackers, and use the believers’ witness to draw persecutors to himself. For more ways to pray for the persecuted church, grab a copy of Pray the World , a 31-day devotional for hard to reach nations.

title: Standing with Brothers and Sisters We Cannot See
summary: David Platt shares a powerful story of forgiveness and challenges Christians to support persecuted believers through prayer.
summary_zh: 大卫·普拉特（ David Platt ）分享了一个关于宽恕的强大故事，并挑战基督徒通过祈祷来支持受迫害的信徒。
title_zh: 与我们看不到的兄弟姐妹站在一起
content: I remember the first time I stood at the demilitarized zone, or the DMZ, on the border between North and South Korea. I looked across this dividing line, knowing that on the other side I (and we) have brothers and sisters who are suffering and dying for following Jesus and making him known. I think about Soon Yangown, a pastor in a leper colony during the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula many years ago. He refused to worship the shrines that had been set up for the Korean people to worship, so he was arrested and imprisoned. When the Japanese occupation ended, he was released. Years later, his two oldest sons, Tongin and Tongsin, were in middle school when a mob representing the communist party came to their campus. The boys were known to be strong Christians, so the mob brought them out of the school and began to beat them. Eventually, a leader of the mob named Ahn shot and killed both the boys. By the time Pastor Soon heard of his sons’ death, the revolt had been quieted, and his sons’ killer had been apprehended. Upon hearing this news, Pastor Soon immediately sent a messenger to the court to plead for them to spare Ahn. The judge agreed to do so, and Pastor Soon then offered to adopt Ahn as his own son. Years later, communists invaded the leper colony where Pastor Soon was pastoring. He refused to flee and chose to stay with the church. He was arrested, imprisoned, tied up with 75 other followers of Jesus, and executed. I wish these stories were only from the past. Unfortunately, however, suffering, persecution, and martyrdom are present-day realities for our brothers and sisters in North Korea. So what can we do for them? For starters, we can remember them and learn about what they are experiencing. In the words of Hebrews 13:3: “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you also are in the body.” We can take time to listen to and learn the story of our family in North Korea as if we were with them in North Korea. (Radical’s documentary Hard to Reach: North Korea is a good place to start.) As you remember our brothers and sisters in North Korea and other hard lands , I invite you to pray for them. Let your prayers be guided by Paul’s exhortation in Ephesians 6:18–20 for the church to pray for him while he was in prison: “To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints, and also for me, that words may be given to me in opening my mouth boldly to proclaim the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains, that I may declare it boldly, as I ought to speak.” Finally, let’s join them. They’re giving their lives to share the gospel with people around them. If you’re reading this, the likelihood is that your life is not at stake in the same way as theirs. But you can still give your life to what they’re giving their lives to: speaking the gospel and sharing God’s love in Jesus with the people you and I interact with today. Let’s lock arms with our brothers and sisters in North Korea , following Jesus and making him known no matter what it costs, because we know that he is our reward. content_zh: 我记得我第一次站在非军事区,即位于南北朝鲜边境的非军事区。 我越过了这个分界线,知道在另一边,我(和我们)有兄弟姐妹,他们因追随耶稣并让他出名而受苦受难并死去. 我想起在多年前日本占领朝鲜半岛期间,一个麻风病殖民地的牧师Soon Yangown。 他拒绝为朝鲜人民所崇拜而设置的神社,于是被捕入狱. 日本占领结束后被放出. 多年后,他的两个最年长的儿子通仁和通辛在中学就读,当时一个代表共产主义政党的暴徒来到了他们的校园. 男孩们已知是坚固的基督徒,于是暴徒将他们从学校带出并开始殴打他们. 最终,一个暴徒的领袖命名 安开枪打死了两个男孩 在Sonon牧师听到他儿子的死讯时,叛乱已经平息,杀害他儿子的凶手已被逮捕。 在听到这个消息后,索恩牧师立即派使者去朝廷恳求他们放过安. 法官同意这样做,而索恩牧师随后提出收养安为自己的儿子. 多年后,共产主义分子入侵了"索恩牧师"正在作牧师的麻风病人聚居地. 他拒绝出逃,选择留在教堂. 他被逮捕,入狱,被绑起与另外75名耶稣追随者,被处死. 我希望这些故事只是从过去。 然而,不幸的是,对我们北朝鲜的兄弟姐妹来说,痛苦、迫害和殉道是当今的现实。 我们能为他们做什么? 首先,我们可以记住他们,了解他们正在经历的一切。 用希伯来人13:3的话来说:“记住那些在狱中的人,好像在狱中一样,以及那些受到虐待的人,因为你也是在身体里。” 我们可以花时间聆听和学习我们家在朝鲜的故事,就像我们在朝鲜与他们在一起一样. (Radical的纪录片"难去难去":朝鲜是个好起点. ) 我邀请你为他们祈祷。 保罗在《以弗所书6:18-20》中劝告教会在狱中为他祈祷:“为此,请全心全意地为所有圣人祈祷,也为我祈祷,愿为我大胆地开口宣讲福音之谜,因为我是一个被锁住的大使,让我大胆地宣示福音之谜。 最后,让我们加入他们。 他们献出生命与周围的人分享福音。 如果你读到这个, 你的生命可能与他们的生命不同。 你仍然可以把生命献给他们所付出的:说出福音,与你我今天交往的人分享上帝对耶稣的爱。 让我们和朝鲜的兄弟姐妹们握起手来, 这篇文章首次刊登在委员会的双周通讯《激进》上, 今日订阅.

title: Doubt Isn’t the Opposite of Faith — But Certainty Might Be
summary: Maybe you believe in God, but you’re not sure how to respond when someone asks why you do. You call it absolute truth, but you’re not absolutely sure about it. At times, you may have your own doubts about God and Christianity. You probably know someone who is “deconstructing” their faith. They grew up in…
summary_zh: 也许你相信上帝，但当有人问你为什么这么做时，你不确定该如何回应。你称之为绝对真理，但你对此并不完全确定。有时，您可能会对上帝和基督教产生怀疑。你可能认识一个正在“解构”他们的信仰的人。他们成长在……
title_zh: 怀疑不是信仰的对立面—但确定性可能是
content: Maybe you believe in God, but you’re not sure how to respond when someone asks why you do. You call it absolute truth, but you’re not absolutely sure about it. At times, you may have your own doubts about God and Christianity. You probably know someone who is “deconstructing” their faith. They grew up in church, went to a Christian school or were even in ministry, but now they’re not sure what they believe. They’re questioning the very foundations of their faith, and it’s uncomfortable and unnerving. Let me lower your expectations right from the start. You probably won’t get every question answered, and your doubts won’t be eradicated. That’s OK. Accepting Christian truths blindly doesn’t build thick faith. The old bumper sticker that declared, “God said it, I believe it and that settles it,” may have seemed helpful, but it has weakened faith. Each of us has to take ownership of our faith. Believing something simply because someone told you has no depth, and the realizations we uncover on our own terms have the potential to transform our lives. Fyodor Dostoyevsky wrote, “I believe in Christ and confess him not like some schoolboy; but my hosanna has passed through a great furnace of doubt.” From the refining fire of doubt, strong convictions can emerge, forged by pursuing answers to our hard questions. Doubt often gets a bad reputation, especially in church settings, but it can be productive. It can paralyze us, but it can also propel us to seek truth. Seasons of deep doubt and earnest questioning have shaped me spiritually. Questioning has the power to open minds, give rise to new ideas and reveal new horizons. When the World Health Organization declared the COVID-19 outbreak a global pandemic on March 11, 2020, it rocked the world. Instead of going to school, work or church, we sheltered in place. The simple act of hugging a family member, or even being in the same room with them, went from a show of affection to a potential threat to their health. Our mental health deteriorated. According to the World Health Organization, the global prevalence of anxiety and depression jumped by 25%. The pandemic also had an unavoidable impact on people’s thoughts about God. According to the Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, “During the early months of the pandemic, Google searches for prayer relative to all Google searches rose by 30%, reaching the highest level ever recorded.” The researchers estimate that by as early as April 1, 2020, more than half of the world’s population had prayed for an end to the pandemic. The deaths of loved ones spawned doubt about a good God. Even before the pandemic, nearly everyone, including me, went through seasons of wrestling with serious doubts about their faith. That questioning often leads a person deeper into God. Theologian Paul Tillich wrote, “Doubt is not the opposite of faith; it is an element of faith.” Embrace your doubts, ask your questions and seek out truth. Not every question you ask will have a clear answer. Mystery abounds in this life, and some spiritual realities exceed our understanding. But I agree with theologian Peter Abelard when he said, “Constant and frequent questioning is the first key to wisdom…. For through doubting we are led to inquire, and by inquiry we perceive the truth.” Even if you aren’t struggling with doubts right now, it’s easy to dismiss someone else’s questions. You may want to tell them to quit worrying and accept that there are some things we will never understand. And when you’re the one asking, it’s tempting to busy yourself with work, family and hobbies to avoid the issue. It’s easier than ever to dodge serious questions by retreating into our ever-present screens instead of engaging the life around us. Dismissing someone’s fears, or hiding from your own struggles, doesn’t help anyone. I surfaced from my struggle with doubt, during dark days of doctoral work, with a new epistemological humility. After examining many other points of view in the hist
content_zh:
或许你相信上帝, 你称之为绝对真理, 有时候,你可能会对上帝和基督教有自己的怀疑. 你可能知道有人正在“破坏”他们的信仰。

他们成长于教堂, 上基督教学校, 甚至还在部里, 他们质疑信仰的根基, 让我从一开始就降低你的期望。 你可能不会得到每个问题的回答, 没关系。

盲目接受基督教真理并不能建立厚厚的信仰。 贴有“上帝说,我相信而且解决了”的旧保险杠贴纸似乎很有帮助,但它削弱了信仰。 我们每个人都必须拥有我们的信仰。

仅仅因为有人告诉你没有深度 就相信了某些东西 而我们以自己的方式发现的 有可能改变我们的生活 Fyodor Dostoyevsky写道:“我相信基督,并承认他不像一个男孩子;

我的众生,确已从一个可疑的大火中经过。 从疑惑的精炼之火中,可以产生出坚定的信念,通过对我们的难题寻求答案来形成这种信念。 怀疑往往会获得不良的名声,特别是在教堂环境中,但是可以产生效果. 它能使我们瘫痪,但也能推动我们寻求真理。

数季的深刻怀疑和认真的质询 使我精神成形 质问有开放思想的力量,产生出新的思想并揭示出新的地平线. 当世界卫生组织于2020年3月11日宣布COVID-19疫情为全球大流行时,它震撼了世界. 我们不是去上学、工作或教堂,而是在原地避难。

拥抱一个家庭成员,甚至与他们同在一室的简单行为,从亲切的表示到他们健康的潜在威胁. 我们的精神健康恶化了。 世界卫生组织表示,全球焦虑和抑郁症的流行程度猛增了25%. 这种流行病也对人们关于上帝的思想产生了不可避免的影响。

根据《经济行为和组织杂志》,“在大流行的最初几个月里,谷歌搜索祈祷相对于所有谷歌搜索都增加了30%,达到了有史以来的最高水平。” 研究者估计,早在2020年4月1日,世界一半以上的人口都曾为结束这种流行病而祈祷.

亲人的死亡引发了对好上帝的怀疑. 即使在疫情爆发之前,包括我在内的几乎所有人都经历了摔跤季节,对他们的信仰抱有严重的怀疑。 这种质疑往往会让一个人更深入地了解上帝。 神学家保罗·蒂利希写道,“怀疑不是信仰的对立面,而是信仰的一个要素。” 接受你的怀疑, 问你的问题和寻找真相。

不是每个问题都有答案 生活中的谜题很多,一些精神现实超出了我们的理解. 但我同意神学家彼得·阿贝拉德的说法:"持续而频繁的质疑是智慧的第一关键.

因为通过怀疑,我们被引导去询问,通过询问,我们了解真相。” 即使你现在没有在怀疑中挣扎, 你可能要告诉他们别担心 接受一些我们永远无法理解的事情

而当你问起的时候, 忙于工作、家庭和爱好, 更难避免严肃的问题, 放弃别人的恐惧, 或逃避自己的斗争,

我从怀疑的挣扎中浮出水面, 在黑暗的博士工作日子里, 带着一种新的认知谦卑。 在研究了其他许多观点之后

title: The Edge Wrote an ‘Elf’ Sequel. Nobody Knows Why It Never Got Made.
summary: Somewhere out there may be a finished sequel to Elf with The Edge’s name on it. That is the claim Andy Richter made on Obsessed: The Podcast, which says the U2 guitarist wrote a full screenplay for Elf 2. Richter, who had a small role in the 2003 film, said someone reached out to the…
summary_zh: 在某个地方，可能会有一个精灵的续集，上面有The Edge的名字。这是安迪·里希特（ Andy Richter ）在《痴迷：播客》（ Obsessed: The Podcast ）上的说法，其中说U2吉他手为《精灵2》（ Elf 2 ）写了一个完整Richter在2003年的电影中扮演了一个小角色，他说有人联系了……
title_zh: 边缘写了一个“精灵”续集。没有人知道为什么它从来没有被制造出来。
content: Somewhere out there may be a finished sequel to Elf with The Edge’s name on it. That is the claim Andy Richter made on Obsessed: The Podcast , which says the U2 guitarist wrote a full screenplay for Elf 2 . Richter, who had a small role in the 2003 film, said someone reached out to the movie’s producer, Shauna Robertson, to tell her The Edge had written a sequel and wanted to talk to her about it. He called it the weirdest story and said the script was apparently fully written. “There is an Edge-penned Elf 2 out there,” he said. The meeting never happened. Robertson was willing to take it, Richter said, and then the whole thing petered out. He did not say when the approach was made or what the story is about, and everything known about the script so far comes from his retelling of a call Robertson received. Hear Richter tell it: Fans have asked for an Elf sequel for more than two decades. One came close in 2013, before Will Ferrell decided not to return as Buddy. Richter said on the same podcast that a sequel would cost far more now than the original did, because Ferrell and director Jon Favreau have since become some of the biggest names in Hollywood and neither of them got a cut of the original’s back end. The Edge has a Christmas record of his own. U2 recorded “Christmas (Baby Please Come Home)” in 1987, and it is still a fixture of holiday playlists. Whether his Elf script includes a version of that, or a song from the band, is anyone’s guess.
content_zh:
在某个地方, 这就是安迪·里克特在"迷信"(The Podcast: The Podcast)上的说法,他说U2吉他手为精灵2写了完整的剧本. 在2003年电影中扮演小角色的里克特说,有人联系了电影的制片人肖娜·罗伯逊,告诉她"边缘"已经写出续集,想和她谈谈这件事.

他称其为"最怪的故事"并称剧本显然已完全写出. 他说,“外面有一只被囚禁的精灵2号”。 会议从未举行. 罗伯森愿意接受,里希特说, 然后整件事就完了.

他没有说这个方法是什么时候作出的,或者故事的内容是什么,而目前为止对剧本所知的一切都来源于他对罗伯逊接到的电话的重述. 听里希特说:粉丝们要求一部精灵续集20多年之久. 2013年,威尔·费雷尔决定不再以"巴迪"的身份回归之前,其中一人接近.

Richter在同一个播客上说,一部续集现在比原作的成本要高得多,因为Ferrell和导演Jon Favreau从此成为好莱坞的一些最出名的人物,两人都没有得到原作后端的切口. "边缘"拥有自己的圣诞纪录. U2于1987年录制了“圣诞节(婴儿请回家)”,它仍然是节日播放列表的固定版本。

他的精灵剧本是否包含这个版本,

title_zh: Dashboard Confessional正在25周年之际将其“MTV Unplugged”设置在路上
content: The most famous night in Dashboard Confessional’s history is going back on tour. The band announced a 15-date North American run celebrating the 25th anniversary of its 2002 MTV Unplugged performance, starting March 12 in Chicago at The Salt Shed and ending April 3 at The Masonic in San Francisco. Chris Carrabba said he wants the shows to carry the spirit of that night. He called the original performance a pivotal and unifying moment for the band and its fans, and said he will play the band arrangements from the original Unplugged set. He has recently played small solo acoustic shows in Nashville, New York and Los Angeles, and said the energy in those rooms is what he wants to bring to bigger venues. The recording that came out of the MTV session, MTV Unplugged 2.0 , was released Dec. 17, 2002 on Vagrant Records as a CD and DVD package and was the band’s first live album. It reworked songs from The Swiss Army Romance and The Places You Have Come to Fear the Most, and “Screaming Infidelities” was its single. The dates: Chicago (Mar. 12), Minneapolis (Mar. 13, The Fillmore), Toronto (Mar. 15, Massey Hall), Brooklyn (Mar. 17, Brooklyn Paramount), Boston (Mar. 19, MGM Music Hall at Fenway), Washington, D.C. (Mar. 20, The Anthem), Philadelphia (Mar. 21, The Fillmore), Atlanta (Mar. 23, Tabernacle), Nashville (Mar. 24, The Pinnacle), Austin (Mar. 26, United Heritage Hall), Dallas (Mar. 27, South Side Ballroom), Denver (Mar. 29, Mission Ballroom), Phoenix (Mar. 31, Celebrity Theatre), Los Angeles (Apr. 1, Hollywood Palladium) and San Francisco (Apr. 3). Tickets go on sale Nov. 13 at 10 a.m. local time through Ticketmaster. Dashboard Confessional is also booked to open for Hilary Duff on her 2027 Lucky Me Tour, which starts in October.

title_zh: “60分钟”问特朗普是否可以原谅他的敌人进入天堂： “答案是否定的。”
content: In a 60 Minutes interview that aired Nov. 8, New York Times columnist Ross Douthat asked President Trump what happens to him when he dies. “Well, I’m a religious person, so in theory, I go to heaven,” Trump said. Asked whether he thinks he’s going, he answered, “Uh, I hope so. I don’t want to go to hell.” Douthat then brought up Charlie Kirk’s memorial service in September 2025, where Erika Kirk spoke about Christian forgiveness and the call to forgive your enemies. Douthat recalled that Trump, speaking after her, had said, “I hate my opponents and I don’t want the best for them.” It was “a little bit of a joke,” Douthat said, “but I think facts come through jokes.” He set the terms: suppose Trump passes away, and all he has to do to enter paradise is feel love and forgiveness for James Comey, Nancy Pelosi and anyone else he has expressed hate for over the years. “Do you think you can do it?” “Well, then I wouldn’t be real, would I?” Trump said. “I mean, if I said to you, sure, the easy answer to that, oh, yes, I could forgive. No, I don’t think it’s an easy question. I found them to be extremely dishonest people. Very bad people. Very bad for our country.” Douthat asked, “Is the answer no?” “The answer is no,” Trump said. “I want to be honest.” He added that he thought they were “very bad people,” and that “I can use the word hate. I do hate some of my enemies. I think they’ve been terrible. Look what they put me through. The weaponization.” Douthat pushed once more. “Mr. President, you have had the most charmed and remarkable life of any American in my entire lifetime,” he said, and asked whether before the judgment throne of God Trump couldn’t find it in his heart to forgive some of his enemies. “After all that’s been given to you. Come on, help me out here. I mean, it’s such an easy answer. All I have to do is say yes, I can.” “I don’t think it’s an easy answer,” Trump said. “Can I be honest? I probably cannot do that now because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will.” Douthat’s final question was framed around the afterlife too. A hundred years from now, “while you’re working out your situation in purgatory,” what is the one line his presidency will be remembered by? “That I made America great again,” Trump said. The exchange came at the end of an interview that mostly covered the midterms, which gave Democrats control of the House and Senate. It also landed with a particular audience in mind. Exit polls after the Nov. 3 election found that 82% of white evangelical voters backed Republican House candidates, the same share as two years earlier, while Catholics and voters with no religion moved toward Democrats. That bloc has stayed with Trump through two elections. Forgiving enemies is one of the plainest commands in the Gospels. In Matthew 5, Jesus tells his followers to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them. In Matthew 6, he says that if we forgive others their trespasses, our heavenly Father will forgive us, and that if we don’t, he won’t. Watch the interaction here:

title: Dr. Derwin Gray: Healing From Trauma Takes Both Jesus and a Good Counselor
summary: Whenever the pilot announced the descent into San Antonio, Dr. Derwin Gray’s eye would start to twitch. This was in his twenties and early thirties, and the twitch lasted as long as he was home. He loves his family. He didn’t know what his body was doing. San Antonio is also where he was sexually…
summary_zh: 每当飞行员宣布降落到圣安东尼奥时， Derwin Gray博士的眼睛就会开始抽搐。这是他二十多岁和三十出头的时候，只要他在家，抽搐就会持续下去。他爱他的家人。他不知道自己的身体在做什么。圣安东尼奥也是他性生活的地方……
title_zh: 德温·格雷博士：治愈创伤需要耶稣和良好的辅导员
content: Whenever the pilot announced the descent into San Antonio, Dr. Derwin Gray’s eye would start to twitch. This was in his twenties and early thirties, and the twitch lasted as long as he was home. He loves his family. He didn’t know what his body was doing. San Antonio is also where he was sexually abused as a child, and where he saw violence growing up. Gray, a pastor and former NFL player who leads Transformation Church in South Carolina, now calls the twitch a trauma response. He wrote his new book, It’s Time to Heal , for people carrying the same kind of wound. “Trauma is more than just something bad happened to you,” he says. “Trauma is something that happens in you, in your nervous system.” Home was the place where he had been abused and had seen domestic violence, and where he had been stopped by police. “So my body was on high alert,” he says. “It was going, ‘You’re going back into an unsafe environment.'” Learning to answer that alarm took years. “I am safe in Christ,” he says he tells himself now. “I’m loved in Christ. I’m not that little child anymore. I can defend myself. I can protect myself.” It took his teenage son to point out another one. A few years ago, the boy noticed that his father’s voice changed whenever he talked to his mother. Gray was patient with everyone else, but not with her. He asked for examples, and his son had plenty. “You’re right,” Gray told him. “I think I’m reacting to a little boy that felt neglected. A little boy that wanted his mom and parents to come to a game.” That boy had been hurt that they seemed to show up only for NFL games. “I need to forgive that,” Gray says, “and that was a part of my healing process.” It is also what he means when he talks about advocating for yourself, which some church cultures hear as selfish. For Gray, it means going back and speaking to the six-year-old he was, who was abused by a 15-year-old boy. “I can say, ‘Derwin, that was not your fault,'” he says. “‘What happened to you was wrong, but that’s not the end of your story.'” Jesus Created Counselors Too Gray has little patience for the idea that therapy is a failure of faith. He has sat in coffee shops with people who walked away from Christianity after being told they didn’t really have depression. “Depression is not a sign that you’ve sinned,” he says. “It’s a sign that we’re sick. We need a doctor. Jesus created medicine. Jesus created therapists. Jesus created counselors.” In his telling, God most often heals through a clinical specialist or a counselor, and also through wise spiritual directors and medication. The theology he can’t abide is the opposite: “ugly and heinous theology that says if you don’t get better, it’s your fault.” The goal, he says, “is not to get better. The goal is to be with a loving God who wants to shepherd you in the process.” What gets under his skin, he admits, is how selective the pray-it-away crowd can be. The same people, he notes, “go on an international missions trip, [and] they have Band-Aids all up and down their shoulders from getting immunization shots.” “Sometimes we the Church are our own worst enemies,” he says. “The dark powers often do more damage to people from people in the church than outside of the church, because we have not had a healthy view of how God wants to heal our minds, how God wants to heal our bodies.” The Pastor at the Door at 4 A.M. Early in ministry, Gray was preaching about grace at a summer camp alongside another pastor, and teenagers spent hours confessing. Around four in the morning came a knock at his door. It was the other pastor, a man who had spoken at the biggest churches and written the books. He confessed that he was watching porn between services. Gray listened for about an hour, then told him what he saw. “You think ministry success is gonna fix your broken heart,” he said. “And it hasn’t.” The man got angry. Gray, who says he’s 5’11” and 200-something pounds, held his ground. “You have idolatry. You think your ministry succes
content_zh:

格雷是一名牧师和前NFL球员,他领导了南卡罗来纳州的转型教堂,现在称抽搐是创伤反应. 他写了一本新书, 他说,“trauma不仅仅是发生在你身上的坏事。”

title_zh: 乔尔·斯莫尔伯恩和他的兄弟刚刚制作了一部关于战争兄弟的电影
content: At one point, Joel Smallbone and his brother Ben went their separate ways. “You could argue we ended up on our own sort of opposite sides of life’s battlefield,” Smallbone says. What brought them back together was a movie about the same thing. “I remember saying, wouldn’t it be fascinating if two brothers who’ve had ideological differences and creative differences came back together behind the camera to tell a story about two brothers that end up on opposite sides of a literal war?” That movie is Drummer Boy , a Revolutionary War Christmas musical that opened in theaters Nov. 6. Joel and Ben co-directed it, and Joel plays Jeremiah Clem. The cast includes Ioan Gruffudd and Melora Hardin (Jan from The Office) . It took a while. Smallbone, who sings in for KING + COUNTRY with his brother Luke, pitched it to Lionsgate on March 10, 2020, and, by his account, the studio nearly greenlit it. “And then March the 13th happened and the world shut down,” he says. Unsung Hero came first and the musical waited. Someone eventually reminded him 2026 is America’s 250th birthday. “Well, maybe it was just always meant to be now.” The Movie That Wrote Him “Do you write the movie or does the movie write you?” Smallbone asks. “There’s never been a movie that’s written me more than Drummer Boy .” He lists the evidence. “We came up with this rendition of ‘The Little Drummer Boy’ at the beginning of our career. We’re called for KING + COUNTRY, which is a British mantra. We wore these revolutionary-type uniforms for many years. I’m in a band with my brother. This is a movie about brothers on opposite sides of the battlefield. I’m a musician. It’s a musical. You just see all of these breadcrumbs.” When he got stuck on the lead character, a director asked him who he was. “I’ve got a rescuer complex,” he says. “A bit of a savior complex. And so I just wrote all of it into the film.” Unsung Hero was literally about his family, so it’s fair to ask why this one feels more like him. His answer is allegory. “Jesus was the allegory guy,” Smallbone says. “He made up stories for a living, you know? I see myself more in it because it’s all allegorical about our life, and America, and me being an immigrant and in a mixed marriage, and brothers on other sides of the battlefield.” A Musical for People Who Hate Musicals “I need to clear up something to the musical haters,” he says. About 30 minutes of the film are musical moments, “very personal expressions of heartache or love or loss.” He calls it “ Hamilton meets The Patriot meets Pride and Prejudice .” His rule for when a character should sing is simple. “The best musicals put language to things that you couldn’t express through dialogue. The worst musicals just sing the whole time. And I’m like, just stop. That’s not life.” His example is Chris Martin writing “Fix You” after Gwyneth Paltrow’s father died. “You have to express yourself in grief, in pain, and a lot of times it comes through music.” The same logic runs through the film. One character, an enslaved woman, sings her way through being stuck. “She’s stuck and she’s enslaved and she needs to sing about it to understand it better,” he says. Two Brothers Behind the Camera The shoot gave the co-directing brothers plenty of challenges to overcome. The last day of filming was the big argument between Jeremiah and Emmaline on a hillside, in 40 mph winds. “She’s in this dress, almost getting blown off the hillside,” Smallbone says. “We were like, I don’t know if we’re gonna use any of this.” The wind made the cut. “The tragedy of the bad weather actually created a third layer to the scene.” The argument matters to the story. Jeremiah, Smallbone says, is “not practicing what he’s preached.” His father taught him “no boy or girl or slave or free, because all in one in Christ are we,” an echo of Galatians 3:28. Jeremiah is “chasing, basically, imperialism and hierarchy and climbing the ladder by who he’s gonna marry.” Heat was the opposite problem. On a day he puts

title_zh: 想要帮助消除贫困吗？这里有五种方法可以开始
content: In the mid-2000s, Ate Tina was working long hours at a factory in the Philippines and supporting her household alone. Ate is Tagalog for older sister, and it’s a title of respect. Seven months after her wedding, her husband developed a serious medical condition, which made her the only breadwinner. When she became pregnant, the factory’s demands stayed the same. “I ended up giving birth at home because I wasn’t allowed to leave work,” she recalls. Two months after her daughter was born, she was back on the factory floor and her daughter was in the care of others. Tina began to notice changes in her daughter’s behavior that worried her. She says she prayed in desperation for a livelihood that would let her provide for her family and be present with them. In 2008, she connected with the Center for Community Transformation, a partner of HOPE International in the Philippines. Her first loan was $80. She repaid it, kept meeting with staff and fellow borrowers, and by her third loan, $800, she bought three sewing machines and rented an apartment to start a sewing business. “Because of that trust, I was able to start a business I can call my own,” she says of the organization that lent to her. The business has since grown into an online clothing company with around 70 employees. Tina trains them, encourages them to save and points them toward the same support she found. The loan mattered. So did the parts of her story that cost nothing: people who trusted her, a group of borrowers who met with her, a prayer life she kept returning to and a skill she kept sharpening. If your budget has no room for a monthly gift, that list is still within reach. Here are five places to start: Watch the way you talk about poverty. Poverty is more than a shortage of money. Material need is real, and it sits inside a larger brokenness that reaches into relationships, communities and a person’s sense of who they are. Talking about poverty that way changes who is in the story. Everyone knows what a broken relationship feels like, so the distance between you and the person asking for help on the corner gets shorter. You make eye contact instead of looking away. You ask a name. You find out what the person actually needs before you decide what to offer. Protect the dignity of the people you want to help. Tina put the turning point in terms of trust. The lender believed she would repay, and she did, and the business that followed was hers. That makes a useful test for any help you offer: does it treat a person as someone with ideas and work of their own, or as someone to be rescued? Giving things away freely is the right call in a crisis. Outside a crisis, it can turn people into recipients in their own community. The better question is how to meet someone’s needs as a whole person while protecting their dignity. Do your job well. You don’t have to work for a nonprofit to fight poverty at work. Vocation is one of the main ways Christians answer the call to love their neighbors, which means many of us are already doing some of that work without noticing. Tina’s sewing business now supports around 70 employees, which is vocation doing exactly this. A barista pours coffee grown by farmers in developing countries. Someone in telecommunications works in an industry that provides cell-phone access in impoverished nations. A worker on an oil field produces fuel that keeps a stranger warm at night. A recruiter connects a person to a job that person badly needs. Pray about where you’ve been placed, do the work well, and think of it as a way to serve people you will probably never meet. Spend your time where the need already is. Poverty has an address close to home, too. Food pantries, tutoring programs and church benevolence ministries run on volunteers, and they tend to need people who show up on a schedule. A standing weeknight shift usually builds more trust than a one-time service day, because the people on the other side get to know your name as well. If you have
content_zh:
2000年代中期,Ate Tina在菲律宾的一家工厂工作了很长的时间,独自养活她的家人. Ate是Tagalog的姐姐, 在她结婚七个月后,她的丈夫发展出严重的健康状况,这使她成为唯一的养家糊口的人. 她怀孕后,工厂的要求保持不变。

她回忆道, “我最后在家中分娩, 女儿出生后两个月,她回到了工厂地板上,她的女儿在别人的照顾下. 蒂娜开始注意到她女儿担心自己行为的变化. 她说,她绝望地祈求生计,使她能够养活家人,并与家人同在。

2008年,她与HOPE国际在菲律宾的合作伙伴社区转型中心建立了联系. 她第一次贷款是80美元。 她偿还了这笔钱,不断与员工和同僚借款人会面,通过第三次贷款800美元,她买了三台缝纫机并租了一套公寓来开办缝纫业务.

“由于这种信任,我得以开办一个我可以称为我自己的企业,”她说,是借给她的组织。 该行从此发展为一家有约70名员工的在线服装公司. 蒂娜训练他们,鼓励他们保存并指向她找到的同样支持. 贷款很重要。

她的故事中那些没有付出任何代价的部分也一样: 相信她的人, 一群与她相遇的借款人, 她不断回归的祈祷生活, 以及她不断磨炼的技能。 如果你的预算没有月度礼物的空间,那名单仍然可以拿到. 这里有五个开始的地方: 注意你谈论贫穷的方式。 贫穷不仅仅是缺乏资金。

物质需求是真实的,它存在于更大的断裂之中,这种断裂涉及到关系、社区和一个人对自身身份的感觉。 说到贫穷 那样会改变故事中是谁 每个人都知道一个破碎的关系是什么感觉,所以你和在角落寻求帮助的人之间的距离会缩短. 你用眼睛接触而不是看不见

你问个名. 在你决定要提供什么之前,先找出这个人实际需要什么. 保护你想要帮助的人的尊严。 蒂娜把转折点 以信任。 贷款人相信她会报答她,她会报答她,随后的生意是她的。

这对你提供的任何帮助都是一种有益的考验:它是把一个人当作有想法和工作的人,还是当作要被拯救的人? 在危机中,自由放弃事物是正确的号召。 在危机之外,它可以把人们变成自己社区的受援者。 更好的问题是,如何满足个人整体的需要,同时保护他们的尊严。 做好你们的工作

你不必为非营利组织工作, Vocation是基督徒响应爱邻居号召的主要方式之一,这意味着我们许多人已经在做一些没有注意的工作. 蒂娜的缝纫行业支持大约70名员工, 一个酒吧为发展中国家农民所种植的咖啡倒灌.

电信业的某个人在贫穷国家提供手机接入的行业工作。 油田上的工人生产出能让陌生人在晚上保持温暖的燃料. 招募者将一个人与他急需的工作联系起来。 祈祷自己被安置在何处, 做得很好,

把时间花在需要的地方 贫穷也有一个离家很近的地址。 食物裤、辅导计划和教会慈善部都以志愿者为对象,他们往往需要按期出现。 每周上夜班通常比一次服务日更能建立信任,因为另一边的人也了解你的名字。 如果你有的话

title: Claire Rosinkranz Heard God at 11. Now She’s Learning to Hear Him Differently
summary: Six years after a ukulele song made her a TikTok phenomenon, the pop songwriter is learning to hear God differently — and to be okay living in the middle.
summary_zh: 在一首尤克里里歌曲使她成为TikTok现象的六年后，这位流行歌曲作者正在学习以不同的方式聆听上帝—并且可以在中间生活。
title_zh: 克莱尔·罗辛克兰兹（ Claire Rosinkranz ）在11岁时现在，她正在学会以不同的方式倾听他的声音
content: Claire Rosinkranz is trying to describe what the last few years have felt like, and she keeps landing on the same word: momentum. Not the kind she chased. The kind that showed up on its own, at 16, and never fully let her catch up to it. “It feels really good, honestly it’s kind of hard to understand how it feels at all,” she says backstage at a music festival. “When I was 16 I had a lot of crazy momentum, and I’ve been telling my team, I just didn’t realize anything that was happening. And so I still feel like I don’t know what’s happening. But I get to sing and dance.” “Backyard Boy” turned a California teenager with a ukulele and a home studio into one of pop’s more unlikely breakouts, a song that racked up millions of TikTok recreations before she’d finished high school. Rosinkranz was already a lifer by then. She’d been writing songs since she was 8 and training as a ballerina before deciding, at 11, that music was the thing. Now 22, with two albums behind her, she is still working out what it means to have built a career on momentum she never planned for. “I gotta learn a lot of patience,” she says. The success of that first song, she says, set her expectations in a way she’s been unwinding ever since. “I ended up getting a lot of success from that song, and so all I knew was success when it came to music,” she says. “So feeling that kind of ebb and flow has been a challenge.” The deeper lesson has been separating who she is from what she makes. Someone in her life has been trying to drill it into her that her worth doesn’t live in her output. “My identity is not in what I do, but in who I am,” she says. “That can be really hard when you get compliments and value from everything that you do in this world. I’m still learning that there’s a lot of ebbs and flows in this industry, and learning how to be in the middle of that.” Being in the middle of things is a phrase she comes back to more than once, and it stretches past her career into how she talks about God. She grew up with a faith that felt less like a decision than a default setting. “God was kind of in my nature,” she says. “Religion was a little bit more like taught to me.” The distinction matters to her more now than it used to. She describes a recent conversation with her therapist in which she admitted she doesn’t hear God the way she once did, half expecting to be told something was wrong. “I was like, I feel like I don’t hear God that much or in the way that I used to, and she was like, I actually don’t completely agree,” Rosinkranz says. “I think that you maybe just hear God differently. I really resonated with that.” Lately, she’s been wondering whether the change is less about losing God’s voice than learning its new frequency. “I’m really learning how to be in the middle of a lot of things, and being okay with being a little bit more fluid instead of having this really crazy concept of right and wrong,” she says. “I feel like I’m a little bit more black and white than I would like to acknowledge, and you can’t really have a lot of growth or change if you don’t.” Her spiritual life shows up in practical, almost mundane ways. Yoga, horseback riding, long afternoons at the beach. She talks to God the way other people talk to a friend, and she asks for dreams, treating them as ground she can meditate from. But the clearest version of the story lives in a memory she comes back to whenever she needs to remember why she’s doing any of this. She was 11, in the back of her cousin’s car, weighing a choice between two loves: ballet and music. “I was sitting there and I was like, God, am I gonna do dance or music, because I was also very passionate about ballet,” she says. “I swear that I heard this other voice that wasn’t myself. That is the thing and the voice that has honestly carried me to where I am today.” She went straight to her mother afterward. “I heard God in a way that I haven’t heard before,” she remembers telling her. “It’s really cool to see everything
content_zh:
克莱尔·罗辛克兰兹(Claire Rosinkranz)试图描述过去几年的感受,她不断以同一个词来登陆:"动力". 不是她追求的那种 那种在16岁的时候独自出现 却从未完全让她赶上 在音乐节的后台,

“当我16岁时, 我有很多疯狂的动力, 所以我仍然觉得自己不知道发生了什么。

但我可以唱歌跳舞。 “Backyard Boy ” ( Backyard Boy ) , 将一个带着一首乌克勒和一家家庭工作室的加州青少年变成了一个更不可能突围的流行作曲家,这首歌在她读完高中之前就挤出数百万个TikTok娱乐。 罗辛克兰兹那时已经是个活人了 她从八岁起就开始写歌,

现在22号,她身后有两张专辑,她仍然在想着在她从未计划过的动力上建立事业的意义. 她说,“我必须学会很多耐心。” 她说,第一首歌的成功使她的期望定下来,从那时起,她一直没有变。 “我最后从这首歌中获得了很多成功,

“因此,感到这种喘息和流动是一个挑战。” 更深刻的教训是 将她是谁 与她所做的。 她一生中有人一直试图钻入她身上, “我的身份不在于我的工作,而在于我是谁。” “当你从你在这个世界上所做的一切中获得赞美和价值时,那会很难。

我仍然在学习这个行业中有很多东西, 身处中间是她不止一次的复出语句,从她的职业生涯延伸到她如何谈论上帝. 她长大时的信仰 感觉不像是决定 她说,“上帝是我的天性。”

“宗教更像是教我的。” 区别对她来说比以前更重要 她描述最近与治疗师的谈话, 她承认自己听不到上帝的旨意,

”罗辛克兰兹说, “我认为你也许只是听到上帝不同的声音。 我确实对此有共鸣。” 最近,她一直在想,改变是否与其说是失去上帝的声音,不如说是学习新的频率。

“我真的在学习如何在很多事情中间,

“我觉得我比我想承认的要黑白一点, 她的精神生活以实用,几乎平庸的方式出现. 瑜伽,骑马出行,长午入海. 她跟上帝说话 就像别人跟朋友说话一样 她要求做梦 把他们当作可以冥想的地面

但最清晰的剧本仍停留在记忆中, 她当时11岁,在她表哥的车后座上,权衡了两种爱的选择:芭蕾和音乐. “我坐在那,我就像,上帝,我要跳舞还是音乐,因为我对芭蕾也非常热情。”

「我发誓, 我听到另一个声音, 这就是真正把我带到今天这个地步的事物和声音。” 之后她直接去找了母亲. 她记得曾告诉她, “看到一切真的很酷。

summary_zh: 当以赛亚第一次进入他的脑海时， N.T.赖特是一个合唱团的男孩，唱着汉德尔的弥赛亚。他说， “安慰，安慰我的人民”和“他因我们的违规行为而受伤”成为他精神家具的一部分，家具留下来了。在他十几岁的时候，他非常喜欢这本书，以至于可以考虑读旧约博士学位。……
title_zh: N.T.赖特：基督徒需要一个比我们大多数人所描绘的更大的神
content: N.T. Wright was a boy in a choir singing Handel’s Messiah when Isaiah first got into his head. “Comfort, comfort my people” and “He was wounded for our transgressions” became part of his mental furniture, he says, and the furniture stayed. By his teens he loved the book enough to consider an Old Testament PhD. He chose Romans instead, partly because Paul quotes Isaiah constantly and gave him a lifelong excuse to keep going back. His new book Into the Heart of Isaiah: The Meaning and Message of Isaiah 40-55 is what came of it, a walk through sixteen chapters he calls one of the most extraordinary poems ever written. If they had been dug out of a scroll in the sands of Libya or Jordan, he told RELEVANT, the whole world would put them on the front page. “This is an amazing piece of writing.” Because they sit in the middle of the Old Testament, he says, many readers just think “bit of the Bible, not sure what that’s about.” He reads them three ways: as the ancient Israelites heard them, as Jesus and the apostles used them, and as they speak to the Church now. Starting with the first, Wright says, “gives us a kind of stability to any other interpretations we then come to.” Some of the best-known lines in American Christianity come from these chapters, including “Mount up with wings as eagles” and “No weapon formed against thee shall prosper.” Wright says anyone reaching for that second verse should remember that an enemy may be claiming the same verse for themselves. After all, in the First World War, British and German forces sang some of the same hymns and claimed the same God’s protection. Context helps, he says, even if we never get all of it. These chapters are addressed to a people exiled for their sin and told that God has dealt with it. Read them as a promise about my success, my salvation, a happy marriage or a thriving business, and “that’s not the story that those verses belong to.” God can give those things, he says, usually inside a larger story about belonging to a people sent to the world, which “may involve pain, suffering, renunciation, et cetera, as well as fulfillment. But let’s never imagine that they’re the whole thing.” He starts the exile story with Adam and Eve, the first people sent out of the garden, and says Israel was the people called to rescue the whole human race, which is why exile brought despair. A people in that position needs forgiveness as well as a way home. The center of the passage, as he reads it, is that God, who had left Jerusalem and the temple to their fate, “is coming back himself in person to sort it all out.” The New Testament applies the same words to John the Baptist getting ready for Jesus. War, Money and Sex Asked whether exile describes the Church now, Wright says he is careful. Five centuries ago Martin Luther wrote about the Babylonian captivity of the Church and cast himself as the one leading it home, a story Wright calls a gross oversimplification, one Luther may have come to see as “over-egging the pudding.” Exile follows idolatry, though, so he names the idols he sees: Mars, Mammon and Aphrodite, or war, money and sex. Each one makes demands and shuts down objections. The military needs it, the markets need it, everybody does it. Part of the problem, he says, is that the Western Church “has joined in the worship of war, has joined in the worship of money, has joined in the worship or at least the collusion with erotic love.” He adds that people need money and defense, and that God gave us our erotic selves. “But when you make them idols and when you give them power over you, then as individuals and as a culture and alas as a church, you’re heading for the rocks.” The rebuke he returns to most is about heaven. The idea that Christianity is about a soul going to heaven when it dies, he says, comes from Plato and from writers like Plutarch, a pagan priest, and not from the Bible. “The name of the game in Christianity is that heaven is going to come to earth.” He points to the
content_zh:
N. T. Wright是唱着汉德尔的弥赛亚的合唱团中的一个男孩,当时以赛亚刚入脑. 他说,“安慰我的人,安慰我的人”和“他因我们的过错而受了伤”,成为他精神家具的一部分,家具也留下了。 在他十几岁的时候,他喜欢这本书 足以考虑一个旧约博士。

他选择了罗马人取而代之,部分原因是保罗不断引用以赛亚的话,并给了他终生的借口来继续后行. 他的新书"入以赛亚之心:以赛亚40-55的意义与信息"正是由此而来,他通过16个章节的走来,称这为有史以来最出众的一首诗.

如果从利比亚或约旦的沙子上挖出卷轴,他告诉相关人士,全世界都会把它们放在头版。

“这是一部惊人的著作。” 因为他们坐在《旧约》的中间,他说,许多读者只是认为“圣经的比特词,不知道是什么。 ” 他读了他们三种方式:古代以色列人听到他们,耶稣和使徒使用他们,现在他们向教会说话.

或他们自己。 毕竟,在第一次世界大战中,英国和德军演唱了部分同名颂歌并声称得到同名神的保护. 他说,即使我们永远得不到一切,背景还是有帮助的。 这些章节是针对一个因罪行被放逐的民族的,并告诉上帝已经处理了.

读这些诗句是为了保证我的成功、我的救赎、幸福的婚姻或兴旺的生意,并且“这些诗句不属于这个故事。” 他说,上帝可以给这些东西,通常是在一个关于属于被送到世界的民族的大故事中,“这可能涉及痛苦、痛苦、放弃等等,以及实现。

但让我们永远不要想象, 他以亚当和夏娃为开头的放逐故事,第一批被派出花园的人,并说以色列是被叫来拯救整个人类的人,这就是放逐带来绝望的原因. 处于这种地位的人既需要宽恕,也需要回家。

正如他所读到的,通道的中心是让耶路撒冷和圣殿走向命运的上帝,“正在亲自回来整理一切。” "新约"对浸信会的约翰(John) 准备接受耶稣也适用了同样的话. 战争、金钱和性问题问流亡者是否描述教会,

5个世纪前,马丁·路德(Martin Luther)写了一篇关于巴比伦人对教会的囚禁并把自己当做回家的领头羊,莱特(Wright)称这故事过于简单化,一位路德(Luther)可能已经看成是“过度的布丁了 ” 。 出走虽然跟随偶像,所以取出他所见到的偶像的名字:火星,马蒙和阿佛洛狄忒,或者战争,金钱和性.

每一个都提出要求并关闭反对。 军方需要它,市场需要它,每个人都这样做。 他说,问题的一部分是西方教会“加入了对战争的崇拜,加入了对金钱的崇拜,加入了对金钱的崇拜,或者至少与色情爱相勾结”。 他补充说,人们需要金钱和防卫,上帝给了我们自己的性。

“当你们以偶像为偶像,当你们以个人、文化、教堂为主宰时,你们就走向石头去。” 他回到多数人的责难 是关于天堂的 他说,基督教是关于灵魂去天堂的观念,来自柏拉图和普鲁塔克等作家,是异教牧师,而不是圣经.

“在基督教中,游戏的名称是天堂将降临到地上。” 他说

The campus is called BlackJack, like the range it meets at: Blackjack Sporting Clays, a…
summary_zh: Ocala最新校园的TruLife教堂(TruLife Church), 一些与会者自己带过来,在门边的架子上检查,其他会众检查步行者的方式. 校园被称为BlackJack,就像它遇到的射程: 21点运动克莱斯, a.
title_zh: 带上你的圣经和你的霰弹枪：认识有史以来最多的佛罗里达教堂植物
content: Sunday services at TruLife Church of Ocala’s newest campus come with a soundtrack of shotguns going off in the distance. Some attendees bring their own and check them at a rack by the door, the way other congregations check strollers. The campus is called BlackJack, like the range it meets at: Blackjack Sporting Clays, a shooting facility in Sumterville, Fla. The facility’s owners came up with the idea and asked pastor Michael Kirby about starting a church plant on the property. Kirby has a handy comparison for the place, which has four courses and a cart. “You rent a golf cart and you drive around and shoot clays at all the different posts,” he said. “It’s like playing golf, but you’re playing with a shotgun.” So it’s golf, but the clubs go off. The sanctuary, loosely speaking, is a pavilion enclosed in thick, clear plastic, with mobile air conditioners keeping the cool air in and the wooded views visible. An 80-inch TV and a full sound system play Kirby’s prerecorded sermon three weeks a month, so three Sundays out of four the preacher arrives by screen. He or another TruLife pastor preaches live once a month, and Kirby’s daughter-in-law, Taylor Kirby, leads worship. Seating is about 40. The church held a soft opening a couple of months ago and had its official launch on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Kirby preaching and a picnic lunch afterward. The day before, during a national competitive shooting event at the facility, volunteers handed out flyers and went door to door in the neighborhood, which is outreach with an unusually loud backdrop. The target audience is the person who came to shoot. “We are hoping to attract unchurched people who are coming to BlackJack to do some shooting,” Kirby said. “Maybe they wouldn’t want to go to your typical church, but they decide they could go over here under the pavilion and hang out.” Evangelism by proximity, in other words: set up next to the people with the shotguns and hope they wander over. Some of them already have noticed the music. Kirby says shooters have told him they can hear the worship from the service, and he is counting on it. “They might not come inside yet, but they’ll be out there worshipping in the middle of the grass,” he said. The worship set, it turns out, doubles as the range’s ambient soundtrack.
content_zh:
Ocala最新校园的TruLife教堂(TruLife Church), 一些与会者自己带过来,在门边的架子上检查,其他会众检查步行者的方式. 校园被称为BlackJack,就像它所遇见的射程: 黑杰克体育克莱斯(英语:Blightjack Sporting Clays),是位于弗拉州苏姆特维尔的一个射击设施.

该设施的业主想出了这个想法,问牧师Michael Kirby关于在该地产上开办一座教堂工厂的问题。 柯比对该地进行了方便的比较,该地有四门课程和一辆推车. 他说:「你租一辆高尔夫球车, “这就像打高尔夫, 高尔夫球,但俱乐部会爆炸。

松散的说,圣所是一个被厚厚的,清晰的塑料包裹的展厅,移动式空调保持了凉爽的空气,木质的景色也清晰可见. 一个80英寸的电视和一个完整的音响系统每月三个星期播放Kirby预先录制的布道,

他或另一位特鲁利夫牧师每月传教一次,柯比的媳妇泰勒·柯比领头崇拜. 座位约40. 教堂在几个月前举行了软开放,并于10月25日星期日正式开堂,柯比在教堂传教,之后进行野餐午餐.

前一天,在设施举行的全国竞技射击活动中,志愿者们散发了传单,并在附近挨家挨户地挨家挨户地走来挨户走去。 目标观众是前来拍摄的人. Kirby说,“我们希望吸引前来BlackJack进行射击的无伤大雅的人。”

“也许他们不想去你们典型的教堂, 近处的福音主义,换句话说:用猎枪布置在人民旁边,希望他们漫游. 其中一些人已经注意到了音乐。 Kirby说枪手告诉他,他们可以听到仪式上的礼拜,他指望着它。

他说,“他们可能还没有进屋,但会在草丛中崇拜”。 结果发现,这种崇拜是环境音轨的两倍。

title_zh: “Mogging”是柯林斯词典2026年的年度词汇
content: Your friend’s sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving. That sentence now has a dictionary’s blessing, because Collins Dictionary has named “mogging” its Word of the Year for 2026. Collins defines it as “outperforming or outshining someone or something, which can mean making them look inferior in appearance, confidence or status.” The word is believed to be short for AMOG, “alpha male of the group.” It started around 2016 in bodybuilding culture, where it named the most physically dominant guy in the gym, then turned into a verb and made the rounds in the manosphere. It’s everywhere now and mostly used with tongue firmly in cheek, which is the only way anyone should use a word that started as a locker-room pecking order. Carspreading made Collins’ list, which is what they call carmakers building vehicles longer, wider and heavier with every new model. SUVs were well over half of new car sales in 2025, and the parking bays are feeling it. The job market contributed ghost job, an opening posted by an employer with no plan to hire anyone. Collins cites a UK study finding that around a third of advertised roles fit the description, so if your applications keep disappearing into the void, that may be part of why. The lighter entries were friendslop, low-budget indie games built for playing with friends, and fricy, fruity plus spicy, as in pineapple and mango hot sauces. Bixie is the haircut between a bob and a pixie that Zendaya, Jessie Buckley and Helen Mirren have worn. Then there is P(doom), the percentage chance someone thinks AI brings about the collapse of human civilization, which is a strange thing to find on the same list as a haircut and a hot sauce. Collins writer Rachel Quin said much of the shortlist felt like one big mogging contest, with everything competing to be bigger, hotter and more dramatic than whatever came before. Her takeaway for the year is that resilience and a little fun may be the way through. Somewhere, a sourdough loaf is winning.
content_zh:
你整个周末都用在了你朋友身上, 该句现在有一个词典的祝福,因为柯林斯词典已经将2026年的年词命名为"吞吐".

柯林斯将它定义为“表现优异或超越某人或某物,这可能意味着让他们在外表、信心或地位上显得低劣 ” 。 认为这个词对AMOG来说是短的,“群体中的阿尔法男性”。 它于2016年左右在健美文化中开始,在那里它命名了健身房中身体上最占优势的男生,然后变成了动词,并在manosphere进行了轮回.

这也是人们唯一应该使用一个以更衣室啄门为起点的词。 汽车的普及使得柯林斯成为了榜单,他们称之为汽车制造者,用每一个新车型建造更长,更宽,更重的车辆. SUV在2025年的汽车新销量中远超过一半,停车场也感受到了这种感觉.

就业市场为鬼子提供了工作,这是雇主张贴的空缺,没有计划雇用任何人。 柯林斯引用了英国的一项研究 发现大约三分之一的广告角色 符合描述, 所以如果你的申请 不断消失到空虚,

更轻的条目是朋友游戏, 低预算的游戏 与朋友玩, 和fricy,水果加辣, 如菠萝和芒果热酱。 Bixie是Zendaya,Jessie Buckley和Helen Mirren穿戴的波波和精灵之间的发型.

接下来是P(doom),即有人认为AI带来人类文明崩溃的百分率概率,这与理发和热酱一样在同一个列表中找到是一件奇怪的事情. 柯林斯作家瑞秋·昆(英语:Rachel Quin)说,许多入围名单都感觉像是一场大杂耍大赛,一切竞相比以往更大,更热闹,更戏剧化.

她这一年的外卖是 恢复力和一点乐趣 可能是过去的方式。 某处,一个酸面包正在赢得。
author: RELEVANT Staff

title_zh: 德鲁斯基的金钱饥渴的巨型教会牧师正在获得他自己的Netflix系列， 12月1日首映
content: The megachurch pastor Druski has been playing for laughs is getting a promotion. Netflix announced a multiyear deal with the comedian on Nov. 2, and the first project is Collect & Praise, a semi-scripted series built around that character. It premieres Dec. 1. Netflix describes a show where faith comes second to fortune. A money-hungry pastor and his unpredictable deacon scheme their way through scandal, chaos and controversy. Mike Epps plays the deacon. For Druski, the deal is about scale. In the announcement he said Netflix will give him the resources to build on his comedy and reach “a new global audience,” and his company, 4LIFERS Entertainment, will develop original programming for the service. Netflix is also licensing three of his existing projects, Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy and Coulda Been Records Auditions, along with a selection of his skits. John Derderian, the Netflix VP who oversees Next Gen Content, said Druski “has a gift for building characters that people can’t stop talking about,” and called Collect & Praise “just the beginning.” He started posting skits on Instagram in 2017 and now has nearly 40 million followers across platforms. Along the way he has been a team captain in the Super Bowl LX flag football game, the youngest host in BET Awards history, a TIME100 Next cover star and the top name on Rolling Stone’s list of the most influential creators, all according to Netflix. He has also been to church on screen before, as a co-star of Praise This, the Peacock church musical, and he has appeared in House Party and Livestream from Hell and in music videos for Drake, Jack Harlow and Lil Yachty. RELEVANT last caught him in December, when he and Timothée Chalamet unexpectedly broke into a Kirk Franklin song. He also presented at the NFL Honors, which Netflix says will stream on the service in 2027. Netflix posted an announcement video with the news. Before the series, there is a bigger stage. On Nov. 7, Druski hosts Saturday Night Live, which Netflix says makes him the first digital content creator ever to host the show. The premiere date, Dec. 1, is also Giving Tuesday.
content_zh:
大教堂牧师德鲁斯基 一直在玩笑乐 正在得到晋升。 Netflix在11月2日宣布与喜剧演员达成多年协议,第一个项目是Collect & Loces,这是围绕该角色打造的半标本系列. 它的首映时间是12月1日,Netflix描述了一个信仰次于财富的节目.

一个渴望钱财的牧师 和他的不可预测的执事 策划他们的方式 通过丑闻,混乱和争议。 迈克·埃普斯饰演执事. 对德鲁斯基来说,交易是关于规模的. 在公告中,他说Netflix会给予他资源在他的喜剧的基础上发展,并接触到"一个新的全球观众",他的公司4LIFERS Entertainment将为服务开发原始的节目.

Netflix也为他现有的三个项目颁发许可证, Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy和Coulda Been Records Experiments,以及他的一些滑稽作品.

监督Next Gen Content的Netflix VP(Netflix VP)John Derderian表示, 德鲁斯基“有造就人物的天赋, 他在2017年开始在Instagram上发布滑板,现在跨平台有近4000万追随者.

他曾经是超级碗LX旗下足球赛的队长,是BET奖历史上最年轻的东道主,是Time100的下一位封面明星,也是滚石最有影响力的创造者名单上的顶级名人,都根据Netflix.

他之前也曾作为"赞美之声"(Locus This),孔雀教堂音乐剧的合星,在"House Party"和"Livestream from Hell"以及德雷克,Jack Harlow和Lil Yachty的音乐录影带中出现过. RELEVANT最后一次抓到他是在12月,当时他和Timothée Chalamet意外地闯入了柯克·富兰克林的一首歌.

他还在NFL荣誉赛上亮相,Netflix表示将在2027年上线服务. Netflix发布公告视频与新闻. 在系列之前,有一个更大的舞台. 11月7日,德鲁斯基主持周六晚间直播,Netflix称这让他成为有史以来第一个主持节目的数字内容创作者. 12月1日的首映日也是周二

title_zh: 魔鬼的娱乐使命
content: The following is the substance of a pamphlet published by Archibald G. Brown, a student and then great ally of C. H. Spurgeon in the cause of the gospel in London. Brown here draws attention to a practice that was gaining ground in the churches of his day: that of holding ‘amusements’ of various kinds, which obscured, diverted from, and in some cases replaced the proper ministry of local churches. Brown was savagely attacked in the wake of the publication of the pamphlet, derided as ‘a kill-joy,’ ‘a morbid pietist,’ and ‘a sour bigot.’ His meaning, however, had been deliberately misrepresented. 1 Brown nowhere objects to all amusement per se , but amusement which masquerades as ministry, distracting the church and deceiving needy sinners. While the context in which Brown wrote may be different from ours, we need to hear his burden for a Church—and for Christians—to make a decisive break with the world and its practices. An Evil in the Camp of the Lord DIFFERENT days demand their own special testimony. The watchman who would be faithful to his Lord and the City of his God has need to carefully note the signs of the times and emphasize his witness accordingly. Con­cerning the testimony needed now, there can the little, if any, doubt. An evil is in the professed camp of the Lord—so gross, so brazen in its impudence—that the most short-sighted of spiritual men can hardly fail to notice it. During the past few years it has developed at an ab­normal rate, ever for evil. It has worked like leaven until now the whole lump ferments. Look which way you may, its presence makes itself manifest. There is little if any­thing, to choose between Church, Chapel, or Mission Hall. However they may differ in some respects, they bear a striking likeness in the posters that figure upon and dis­figure their notice boards. Amusement for the people i s the leading article advertised by each. If any of my readers doubt my statement, or think my utterance too sweeping, let them take a tour of inspection and study “the announce­ments for the week” at the doors of the sanctuaries of the neighbourhood; or let them read the religious advertise­ments in their local papers. I have done this again and again, until the hideous fact has been proved up to the hilt, that “amusement” is ousting the preaching of the gospel as the great attraction: “Concerts,” “Entertain­ments,” “Fancy Fairs,” “Smoking Conferences,” “Dramatic Performances,” are the words honoured with biggest type and most startling colours. The burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter The Concert is fast becoming as much a recognised part of church life as the Prayer Meeting, and is already, in most places, far better attended. “Providing recreation for the people” will soon be looked upon as a necessary part of Christian work and as binding upon the Church of God, as though it were a Divine command, unless some strong voices be raised which will make themselves heard. I do not presume to possess such a voice, but I do entertain the hope that I may awaken some louder echoes. Anyway, the burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter, and I leave it with Him to give my testimony ringing tone, or to let it die away in silence. I shall have delivered my soul in either case. Yet the conviction fills my mind that in all parts of the country there are faithful men and women who see the danger and deplore it and will endorse my witness and my warning. Gratifying the Flesh and Retaining a Comfortable Conscience It is only during the past few years that “amusement” has become a recognized weapon of our warfare and de­veloped into a mission. There has been a steady “down grade” in this respect. From “speaking out,” as the Puri­tans did, the Church has gradually toned down her testi­mony; then winked at and excused the frivolities of the day. Then she has tolerated them in her borders, and now she has adopted them and provided a home for them under the plea of “reaching the masses and getting the ear of the

在过去几年里,它以异常的速度发展,永远是邪恶的。 直到现在,它一直工作着,就像离开一样。 看看你们可以走哪条路,它的存在就变得明显了。 教会、礼拜堂或传教堂之间几乎没有任何选择。

然而,它们在某些方面可能有所不同,它们在海报上带有惊人的相似性,这些海报上显示它们的通知板并毁容。 为人民提供娱乐 我是每篇广告的主要文章

如果我的读者怀疑我的发言,或者认为我的言论过于笼统,让他们巡视视察,在附近圣所门口研究“一周的公告”;或者让他们在当地报纸上阅读宗教广告。

在令人发指的事实被证实之前,我一再这样做,即“辱骂”正在驱使福音的传道成为伟大的取景:“关注”、“参与”、“盛会”、“吸烟会”、“戏剧表演”是用最出名和最令人惊叹的颜色表达的言论。

主的重担在我这里 音乐会正迅速成为教会生活中 公认的部分 与祈祷会一样 并且已经,在大多数地方,

“为人民提供娱乐”将很快被视为基督教工作的必要部分,对上帝的教会具有约束力,似乎这是神的命令,除非有人发出强烈的声音,让自己听到。 我并不认为拥有这种声音,但我确实希望能够唤起一些更响亮的回声。

无论如何,上帝的重任 由我负责这件事, 我留给他 让我的证词响亮的语气, 或者让它静静地死去。 无论哪种情况,我都会送出我的灵魂 然而,这一信念使我满怀信心,即全国各地都有忠实的男女看到这种危险并对此感到痛惜,并将赞同我的证人和我的警告。

修行并保持舒适的良知 直到过去几年,“暴行”才成为我们战争的公认武器并发展成一个特派团。 这方面的“级别”稳步下降。 正如普里坦人所做的那样,教会从“大声疾呼”开始,逐渐淡出她的遗言;然后轻视并原谅了今天的纷争。

然后,她在边境上容忍他们,现在她收养了他们,在“影响群众,让人民听到他们的声音”的恳求下,为他们提供了家园。

title: Seven Rules for Catechizing
summary: In our interview with Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn, Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly, he mentions the noted catechist Thomas Lye (1621–1684) and his seven rules for catechizing. Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven […]   The post  Seven Rules for Catechizing  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 在我们对威斯敏斯特议会幕后查德·范·迪克斯霍恩博士的采访中，他提到了著名的教义问答家托马斯·莱（ 1621-1684 ）及其教义问答的七条规则。这里，以无障碍的格式，是Lye对他的七部分方法的解释。虽然一些建议与他出版的问答版本有关，但七[…]后问答的七条规则首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
title_zh: 问答的七条规则
content: In our interview with Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn, Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly , he mentions the noted catechist 1 Thomas Lye (1621–1684) and his seven rules for catechizing. Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven basic steps or rules may be widely applied. The reader should note that Lye was so accustomed to catechising people by means of a ‘question and answer’ method, that even his instructions concerning catechesis are communicated in sequential questions and answers! Introducing the Rules for Catechizing Q. 1. Are there any rules proposed to be observed in catechizing? A. Yes. Q. 2. Is there a title to those rules? A. Yes. Q. 3. Which is the title to those rules? A. A form of examination according to the rules or method proposed to be observed in catechizing. Q. 4. Is catechizing an ordinance? A. Yes. Q. 5. Whose ordinance? Is it God’s? A. Yes. Q. 6. How do you prove it? A. I prove it out of Proverbs 22:6: ‘Train up (or catechize) a child in the way that he [or she] should go, and when they are old they will not [or at least they should not] depart from it.’ Q. 7. How many rules are there to be observed in catechizing? A. Seven. Rule 1: Read and Return Q. 8. Which is the first rule to be observed in catechizing? A. Let the question be barely propounded, and the answer returned. Rule 2: Yes or No? Q. 9. What is the second rule? A. Try the child’s understanding, whether he (she) doth discern truth from falsehood. Q. 10. How shall the child manifest that? A. Only by saying Yes or No, to such short questions as may be raised from the preceding answer. Q. 11. Where are they set down? A. Next to the answers. Q. 12. Why is this necessary? A. Because to repeat words, and not to understand the truths contained in them, is but to act the parrot, and profits very little. Q. 13. But how must the child be made to say Yes or No? A. Without book only. Q. 14. Why then do we use to read them? 2 A. For two reasons. 1. Because we should learn to read them exactly. 2. Because the oftener we do read them, and the better we do consider them, the more capable we shall be to answer them truly without book, if we should (at any time) be so examined. Rule 3: Check the Words Q. 15. What is the third rule? A. Try the child’s ability to express his (or her) knowledge of the meaning of every hard and difficult word or phrase in the preceding answer. Q. 16. What reason is there for this? A. Because we cannot rightly apprehend truths, unless we clearly understand the meaning of those words in which truths are wrapped up. Q. 17. What may be of special use for an help to the child herein? A. The Alphabetical Table at the end of this catechism Q. 18. How may I find any difficult word in the Table? A. Mark with what letter it begins, and then look for it under the same letter in the Table. Q. 19. How may I know the difficult words in the answers? A. Note, that every difficult word explained in the Table is printed with a black English character in every answer. Rule 4: Prove the Point(s) Q. 20. What is the fourth rule? A. Draw the whole answer into several doctrinal propositions (if it contains more than one) and bid the child prove each or either of them by Scripture. Q. 21. Why should the answer be drawn into several doctrinal propositions? A. For two reasons: 1. Because there are several distinct truths contained in several answers of the catechism. 2. Because the more distinctly and particularly any truth is proposed, the more capable the child’s understanding is to apprehend it. Q. 22. Why must the child prove each of these doctrinal propositions by Scripture? A. Because the Holy Scriptures are the only foundation and proof of infallible and saving truth. Rule 5: Observe the Scriptures Q. 23. What is the fifth rule? A. Take the several Scriptures annexed to the answer, and in order propose them distinctly to the child:
content_zh: 他提到著名天主教徒托马斯·莱(1621年-1684年), 以方便的方式, 虽然有部分建议与他所出版的"阴道"版本有关,但七个基本步骤或规则可能被广泛应用. 读者应该注意到,Lye很习惯用 " 问答 " 的方法对人进行分类,甚至连他关于天主教的指示都用顺序问答来传达! 1. 是否提议在授衔中遵守任何规则? A. Yes. Q. 2. 这些规则是否有标题? 问题3. 这些规则的标题是什么? A. 按照拟在编目中遵守的规则或方法进行的检查。 问题4. 对法令进行授衔吗? 问题5. 谁的政令? 是上帝的吗? A. Yes. Q. 6. 你怎么证明? A. 我从 " Proverbs " 22:6中证明: " 训练(或授精)一个儿童,以便他(或她)去,当他们老了,他们不会[或至少他们不应该]离开。 " 问题7. 分类时要遵守多少规则? A.七. 第1条:阅读和返回问题8. 哪些是第一条在编目中遵守的规则? A. 让问题几乎不提,答案就回来了。 规则2:是还是否? A. 试看孩子的理智,无论他从谎言中辨别真理。 问题10. 孩子怎么表现? A. 只有回答是或否,才能回答上文答复中可能提出的简短问题。 问题11. 他们在哪里? A. 答案旁边。 问题12. 为什么有必要? A. 重复这些话,而不是理解其中包含的真理,只是做鹦鹉,利润很少。 问题13. 但如何让孩子说"是"或"否"?. A. 没有书。 问题14. 为什么我们用它来读? 2 A. 原因有两个。 1. 因为我们应当学习准确阅读。 2. 因为我们越经常地阅读,而且我们越看好,如果我们(在任何时候)接受这样的审查,我们就越有能力在没有书的情况下真正回答这些问题。 第3条:检查"字"Q. 第三个规则是什么? A. 尝试儿童表达(或她)对前一个答案中每个困难和困难的词或短语含义的了解的能力。 问题16. 这有什么原因? A. 因为我们不能正确地抓住真理,除非我们清楚地理解那些掩盖真理的文字的含义。 问题17. 向儿童提供帮助有何特别用? A. 本目录末尾的字母表 Q 18. 我怎么才能在桌子上找到任何困难的词? A. 标出它开始的字母,然后在表格的同名字母下查找. 问题19. 我怎么会知道答案中的困难? A. 注意,表格中解释的每个困难字,每个答案中都用黑色的英文字符打印出. 第4条:证明问题20。 第四个规则是什么? A. 将整个答案归纳为几个理论性建议(如果包含一个以上),并让儿童通过《圣经》证明每个或其中之一。 问题21. 答案为何应纳入若干理论性建议? A. 有两个原因: 1. 因为阴道的几个答案中包含有几种不同的真理. 2. 由于所提出的真相越明显,尤其是任何真相,儿童越能理解,就越能抓住真相。 问题22. 为什么孩子必须用"圣经"来证明这些理论命题? A. 因为"圣经"是不可逆和拯救真理的唯一基础和证明. 第5条:遵守"圣经"问题23. 第五个规矩是什么? A. 将答复所附的几本经文取而代之,以便向儿童提出:

summary: Next week marks the launch of a new video and audio resource from the Banner—Westminster Wednesdays. Here Joshua answers some questions about what viewers and listeners […]   The post  What Can I Expect from Westminster Wednesdays?  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 下周标志着Banner-Westminster周三推出了新的视频和音频资源。每周，我们的传播经理约书亚·凯拉德（ Joshua Kellard ）将与一位特邀嘉宾一起，就《威斯敏斯特问答》（ Westminster Shorter Catechism ）中的问题和答案进行深入对话。在这里，约书亚回答了一些关于哪些观众和听众的问题[…]这篇文章“我能从威斯敏斯特星期三期待什么？”首次出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 我对威斯敏斯特周三有什么期待？
content: Next week marks the launch of a new video and audio resource from the Banner— Westminster Wednesdays . Each week our Communications Manager, Joshua Kellard, will be joined by a special guest for an in-depth conversation on the questions and answers contained in the Westminster Shorter Catechism. Here Joshua answers some questions about what viewers and listeners can expect from the series: Are these podcasts just for Presbyterians, or for a wider audience who may not be as familiar with the Shorter Catechism? These podcasts most certainly are for Presbyterians, but not exclusively so! The Westminster Shorter Catechism is an accessible and crisp statement of the Christian faith as it was recovered and clarified at and shortly after the Reformation. Therefore, I would venture to say that any true believer in the Lord Jesus who takes up the Shorter Catechism will find it to be a document that is rich, biblically rooted, encouraging, and edifying. We hope that these podcast episodes are all these things, too. And, I might add, not all our guests are Presbyterians! The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching What does each episode include? How long will each episode last? Each episode of Westminster Wednesdays begins with a reading of the question and answer for that week (sometimes there are two or even three, depending on the topic). Then we have an in-depth conversation on the biblical teaching covered by the question and answer with a special guest—usually a local church pastor, but we have a scattering of seminary teachers represented as well. Above: Some of the Westminster Wednesdays guests. The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching, especially with a view to helping all who listen to teach others in turn. We will often pause, for example, to ask how a father or mother might teach the truths covered on a given week to their children. The episodes are about 15 to 20 minutes in length. There is minimal ‘fluff’—we try to get straight to the topic at hand. How might the series help listeners in their devotions, and as they serve in the church? All biblical truth, seen by the light of faith, should motivate us to thank, praise, and love the Lord more. Given that the Shorter Catechism summarizes scriptural truth for understanding and for devotion, we should be able to see reasons to thank, praise, and stand in awe of God every week. That said, no merely human document should ever take the place of hearing and reading Scripture. The more time anyone spends in a confession or a catechism, the more they should be motivated to return to the Scriptures with fresh perspective and deeper hunger. We also hope the series will be a blessing to churches. For one thing, well–taught Christians are a blessing to the church. They can and should find ways to build up other members in the faith. It may also be the case that we have some pastors and elders watching or listening in. If so, we hope and trust they will be encouraged to consider whether catechesis could be part of their approach to teaching their congregations. Churches that practice both expository preaching and steady catechesis have often found these modes of teaching to be mutually reinforcing. Why did you choose to use the Shorter Catechism as a framework? There are quite a few Reformed catechisms out there, but only a handful are in frequent use today. The Shorter Catechism has the advantage of broad scope (there are 107 questions and answers in this ‘shorter’ document!) coupled with memorable expression. And, as Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn shares in our bonus historical episode Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly (releasing 28 October), each of the questions and answers is a stand-alone unit—one doesn’t have to have read the whole document to understand what is being asked and answered. The reader is often struck by what might clumsily be called the theological or pastoral ‘
content_zh: 下星期将推出来自班纳-威斯敏斯特星期三的新视频和音频资源。 我们的通讯经理Joshua Kellard 每周都会有一位特邀嘉宾参加, 深入讨论威斯敏斯特短卡捷主义的问答。 在这里,约书亚回答了一些关于观众和听众可以从系列中期待什么的问题: 这些播客只是给长老会的,还是给那些可能不太熟悉"更短卡通"的更广大的观众的? 这些播客当然是长老会的, 威斯敏斯特·肖特克·卡特克主义(Westminster Shorter Catechism)是基督教信仰的一种易懂而简洁的表述,因为它在改革期间和之后不久被恢复和澄清. 因此,我冒昧地说,任何真正相信耶稣主的人,如果接受更短的卡德克主义,就会发现它是一份富饶、圣经根基、鼓励和启发性的文件。 我们希望这些播客节目也是这些东西。 还有,我想补充一下,不是所有的客人都是长老会的! 关键在于运用更短的卡德主义来帮助我们理解并应用圣经的教导, 每集会持续多久? 每集"威斯敏斯特周三"以阅读该周的问答开始(有时根据话题的不同会有两集甚至三集). 然后,我们与一位特别的来宾——通常是一位当地教会牧师——深入讨论了问答中包含的圣经教义问题,但我们也有众多神学院教师的代表。 上:一些西敏周三来宾. 重点是利用"更短的卡德克主义"帮助我们理解并应用"圣经"的教义,特别是为了帮助所有倾听者依次教导他人. 例如,我们往往会停下来问,父亲或母亲如何向其子女传授某一周的真相。 剧集长度约15至20分钟. 我们尽量直截了当, 该系列如何帮助听众的奉献,以及他们在教堂中服役? 所有的圣经真理,由信仰之光所见,应该激励我们感谢,赞美,更爱主. 鉴于 " 更短的卡特克主义 " 为理解和奉献总结了文字上的真理,我们应该能够每周看到感谢、赞扬和敬畏上帝的理由。 尽管如此,绝不应仅以人类文件取而代之的是听取和阅读《圣经》。 任何人在忏悔或阴道中花费的时间越多,就越应该以新的视角和更深的饥饿来激励他们回到"圣经". 我们也希望这一系列会给教会带来祝福. 首先,教好基督徒是教会的福分。 他们能够而且应当找到办法,在信仰中培养其他成员。 也可能是有些牧师和长老在看或听。 如果是这样,我们希望并相信,将鼓励他们考虑,天主教会能否成为他们教会的一部分。 既进行说明式传道,又进行平稳天主教的教会往往发现这些教学方式是相辅相成的。 你为什么选择用"更短的卡特主义"作为框架? 那里有很多改革式的天主教,但今天只有很少的宗教经常使用。 Shorter Catechism具有广泛的优势(本文"shorter"文件中有107个问答), 而正如Chad Van Dixhoorn博士在威斯敏斯特大会(10月28日放出)的《幕后新闻》中分享的, 读者常常被俗称神学或牧业所震撼。

title: Pitfalls in Preaching: A Letter on Application
summary: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear […]   The post  Pitfalls in Preaching: A Letter on Application  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 以下信件发表在2025年12月的《旗帜》杂志上。这本书是应一位读者的要求出版的，他认为这本书很有帮助，希望它的忠告也能祝福他人。您也可以在Banner播客上收听这封信的阅读。尊敬的[…]《讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信》（ Pitfalls in Preaching: A Letter on Application ）一文首次出现在美国真理旗帜
title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i
