title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010. title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. From a missionary perspective, she believes the lab addresses a common challenge. “It’s hard to know sometimes as churches how to be a good sending church and how to support missionaries,” she sa
content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. title: African workshop equips communicators
summary: Participants say it will help bring attention to Bible translation movements in their countries.
summary_zh: 参与者表示，这将有助于引起人们对自己国家圣经翻译运动的关注。
title_zh: 非洲工作坊为沟通者提供装备
content: Mike Arthur (GILLBT, Ghana), Daisy Kilel (BTL, Kenya) and Hellen de Bruijn (Wycliffe South Africa) working together at the communication workshop. (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT) Nairobi, Kenya — Participants in a communication workshop say the experience will have a big impact on their work to bring attention to Bible translation movements in their countries. “I believe that communication will bring about a revival in the Bible translation ministry upon my return”, said Adelphe Dogue Syssa, Director for Communication at ACATBA in the Central African Republic. Dogue Syssa was one of 10 participants from across Africa gathered here for a communication workshop from 2-6 November, 2026. The workshop was led by communication staff members serving with several different Alliance organisations in Africa. The site was the BTL’s Christian International Conference Centre near Nairobi. This was the first in-person communication training event in Africa hosted by the Wycliffe Global Alliance in eight years. The workshop’s goal was to equip communication staff, who often take on several roles in their organisations, with the basic skills to serve across different areas of communication. Sessions included communication strategy and planning, interviewing and writing stories, use of design tools, social media and photography. Evans Abade, a communications assistant at BTL East Africa, attended specifically to develop his skills. ‘I want to gain skills in matters of communications’, he said, ‘but I know communication is very broad and we can’t do it alone with the team that we have. So when I heard that we are going to have the team from different organisations […] I thought of this is the best platform for me to gain skills.’ Rather than a single trainer, the workshop brought together staff from the participating Alliance organisations to share their skills and experience. The result was not only new technical knowledge for participants, but also a growing sense of community. ‘Now when I’m interacting with these people, I’m getting to know new ideas’, Abade said. The skills gained and the relationships built during the workshop could have a lasting impact. Dogue Syssa feels motivated to take his newfound knowledge back to the people he serves. CAR has 142 people groups and languages, many of whom do not have full Scripture. ‘Without communication, we cannot appreciate the relevance of the Bible translation’ he said. ‘Communication with churches and communities is essential.’ Isaac Forchie (CABTAL, Cameroon) leads group discussions during the communication workshop (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT) Evans Abade (BTL, Kenya) and Adelphe Dogue Syssa (ACATBA, Central African Republic) share a joke during a break in the sessions. (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT)

Mike Arthur(GILLBT,加纳)、Daisy Kilel(BTL,肯尼亚)和Hellen de Bruijn(Wycliffe,南非)在交流讲习班上合作。 (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT) 肯尼亚内罗毕——一个交流研讨会的参与者说,经验将对他们的工作产生很大影响来引起人们对自己国家圣经翻译运动的注意.

中非共和国基督徒废除酷刑行动组织通信主任Adelphe Dogue Syssa说,“我认为,在我返回后,沟通将使圣经翻译部恢复活力”。 Dogue Syssa是2026年11月2日至6日,来自非洲各地的10名与会者之一。

讲习班由在非洲几个不同联盟组织服务的通信工作人员领导。 该地是BTL在内罗毕附近的基督教国际会议中心. 这是Wycliffe全球联盟8年来首次在非洲举办面对面的通信培训活动。

讲习班的目标是使经常在其组织中起若干作用的通讯工作人员具备在各种通讯领域服务的基本技能。 会议内容包括传播战略和规划、采访和撰写故事、使用设计工具、社交媒体和摄影。

在BTL东非的通信助理埃文斯·阿巴德(英语:Evans Abade (film))专门参加开发他的技能. 他说:「我想获得沟通技巧」,

所以当我听说我们将会有来自不同组织的团队... ... 我认为这是我获得技能的最佳平台。 该讲习班不是单一的培训员,而是汇集了参加讲习班的联盟各组织的工作人员,分享他们的技能和经验。

其结果不仅是参与者掌握了新的技术知识,而且社区意识日益增强。 Abade说, 当我与这些人互动时, 讲习班期间获得的技能和建立的关系可产生持久影响。 Dogue Syssa觉得有动机把他的新知识带回他所服务的人身边.

中非共和国有142个民族团体和语言,其中许多人没有完整的圣经。 他说,“没有沟通,我们就无法理解圣经译文的相关性”。

`与教会和社区的沟通至关重要。 Isaac Forchie(喀麦隆CABTAL)在交流讲习班期间领导小组讨论(摄影师:Mike Arthur/GILLBT)、Evans Abade(肯尼亚BTL)和Adelphe Dogue Syssa(中非共和国ACATBA)在休会期间分享一个笑话。 (摄影:迈克·亚瑟/GILLBT)

title: Alliance seeks next Executive Director
summary: In a time of global challenge and opportunity, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director.
summary_zh: 在这个充满全球挑战和机遇的时代，威克理夫全球联盟正在寻找下一任执行董事。
title_zh: Alliance寻求下一任执行董事
content: God’s Word transforms lives, strengthens churches and brings hope across generations. Bible translation is part of that story, as communities around the world encounter God’s Word in their own languages. Its future calls for leaders who listen deeply, build trust across cultures and empower others. Within this context, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director. Could this be your next calling? The Wycliffe Global Alliance is seeking its next Executive Director to serve a worldwide community of more than 100 organisations united in God’s mission through Bible translation. Th e opportunity : Bring our global community together around a shared vision, strengthen local leadership and help a diverse global movement respond to new opportunities with faith and wisdom. The challenge : Lead through change. Articulate a compelling shared vision, strengthen the support the Alliance offers its organisations, and engage support organisations and financial partners in advancing the work. This calls for leadership that honours local autonomy while strengthening global unity, trust, mutual accountability and financial sustainability. We are looking for a leader who brings: A deep commitment to Jesus Christ and a humble, prayerful approach to leadership. At least five years of senior leadership experience and a relevant master’s degree. Proven ability to lead across cultures, develop leaders and empower local churches. Strategic vision, significant fundraising experience and the ability to turn plans into meaningful outcomes. Emotional maturity, integrity and resilience through change. Feel called—or know someone who might be? Expressions of interest, or candidate recommendations, are welcomed confidentially by 30 November 2026 . More info: full profile and how to respond
content_zh: 神之道会改变生活,加强教堂,并带来世代相传的希望. 圣经翻译是这个故事的一部分,因为世界各地的社区都用自己的语言遇到上帝的话语。 它的未来要求领导人深刻倾听,在不同文化之间建立信任并赋予他人权力。 在这方面,威克里夫全球联盟正在寻找其下任执行主任。 这会不会是你的下一个电话? Wycliffe全球联盟正在寻求下一任执行主任,通过圣经翻译服务于100多个组织联合起来执行上帝的使命。 机会:把我们的全球社会团结在一个共同的愿景周围,加强地方领导,帮助一个多样化的全球运动以信念和智慧应对新的机遇。 挑战:领导变革。 阐述令人信服的共同愿景,加强联盟为各组织提供的支持,并让支助组织和金融伙伴参与推进这项工作。 这要求发挥领导作用,尊重地方自治,同时加强全球团结、信任、相互问责和财政可持续性。 我们要找一位领导,他带来: 对耶稣基督的深刻承诺和谦卑而虔诚的领导方式. 具有至少五年的高级领导经验和相关的硕士学位. 证明有能力领导不同文化,培养领导人并增强地方教会的能力。 战略愿景、大量筹资经验和将计划转化为有意义的成果的能力。 情感成熟,完整性和通过变化的韧性. 感觉被叫了... 还是认识一个人? 在2026年11月30日之前,以保密方式欢迎表示兴趣或候选人建议。 更多信息:完整简介和如何应对

title: Wycliffe Global Alliance Communications Workshop – Africa Area
summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America
summary_zh: 该项目旨在为培训师提供能够在拉丁美洲范围内提供OBT培训的背景知识
title_zh: 威克里夫全球联盟传播研讨会–非洲地区
content: Communication staff at 18 Bible translation organizations across Africa need professional training to tell God’s stories well. In November 2026, a one-week workshop in Ruiru, Kenya will teach practical skills like writing, photography, design and video. Then, six months of follow-up support will continue to strengthen networks and create a collaborative culture of sharing God’s stories widely and effectively. Project Name: Africa Area Communication Capacity Building Workshop Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance – Africa Area Contact: Phil Prior Director for Communication Wycliffe Global Alliance phil_prior@wycliffe.net Matthew Bore Project Funding Manager Wycliffe Global Alliance matthew_bore@wycliffe.net Start date: September 2026 End date: March 2027 Summary Across Africa, God is moving. Communities are receiving the Bible in their own language for the first time. Lives are being transformed. But too often, these stories never become known beyond the place where they happen. Why? Because not enough people are trained to recognise and report these stories to a wider audience. Among 18 Bible translation organisations across Africa, communication staff are doing their best—but without formal training in news writing, interviewing, photography, video and social media. Many also work in relative isolation without the chance to exchange ideas and collaborate on stories. The result: Amazing stories remain untold, and the people who could be praying, giving or getting involved never learn about the opportunities. This project changes that. For one week (2-6 November 2026) in Ruiru, Kenya, communication staff from those 18 Wycliffe Global Alliance organisations will come together — not just to sit in a classroom, but to actually create. Using smartphones and free tools, they will learn to capture the moments that matter: local communities and churches collaborating; a translation team’s challenges and creative solutions, groups engaging with Scripture, lives being transformed. Attendees also will build plans for how their organisations will keep telling these types of stories long after the workshop ends. Then, over the ensuing six months, this same group will keep coaching, encouraging, and learning from each other — turning 18 separate voices into one strong, unified story of what God is doing across Africa. content_zh: 非洲18个圣经翻译组织的传播人员需要专业培训,才能很好地讲述上帝的故事。 2026年11月,将在肯尼亚鲁伊鲁举办为期一周的讲习班,教授写作,摄影,设计和录像等实用技能. 然后,六个月的后续支持将继续加强网络,并创造一种广泛而有效地分享上帝故事的合作文化。 项目名称: 非洲区域通信能力建设讲习班 执行组织: Wycliffe 全球联盟 – 非洲地区联系人: Phil 通讯前主任 Wycliffe 全球联盟 phil prior@wycliffe.net 马修·伯尔项目资金经理 Wycliffe 全球联盟 matthew bore@wycliffe.net 开始日期:2026年9月 结束日期:2027年3月 总结跨非洲,上帝在移动. 社区首次以自己的语言接受圣经。 众生被化. 但是,这些故事往往从未被人们知道,超越发生它们的地方。 为什么? 因为没有足够的人受过训练 来认识这些故事 并向更广泛的受众报告。 在全非洲的18个圣经翻译组织中,通讯工作人员正在尽了最大的努力,但没有接受新闻写作、采访、摄影、录像和社交媒体方面的正式培训。 许多人还相对孤立地工作,没有机会就故事交流和协作。 结果:令人惊奇的故事仍然无穷无尽,那些可以祈祷、给予或参与的人永远不知道机会。 这个项目改变了这一点。 有一个星期(2026年11月2日至6日),来自Wycliffe全球联盟18个组织的通讯工作人员将聚集一堂, 使用智能手机和免费工具,他们会学会抓住重要的时刻:当地社区和教会合作;翻译团队的挑战和创造性解决方案;参与圣经的团体;生活正在被改变。 学员们还将制定计划,说明他们的组织如何在讲习班结束后很久继续讲述这类故事。 然后,在接下来的六个月里,这个团体将继续相互指导、鼓励和学习——把18个独立的声音变成一个强大、统一的故事,讲述上帝在非洲各地正在做什么。 给这个工程 点击 现在给到我们的安全赠送门户。 填表时,您将被要求选择一个项目。 选定非洲区域通信讲习班。 为了了解这个资助机会,

title: Training Oral Translators Across Southeast Asia
summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America
summary_zh: 该项目旨在为培训师提供能够在拉丁美洲范围内提供OBT培训的背景知识
title_zh: 在东南亚培训口译员
content: A three-year training program will prepare local translators across Southeast Asia to put the Bible into spoken forms—like storytelling and song—for communities that share knowledge by voice, not writing. Three workshops will build translators’ skills from basic to advanced to mentoring, so at least 20 participants gain local expertise. Project Name: Training Oral Translators Across Southeast Asia Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance Contact: Evelyn Gan Consultant for Oral Translation Programmes Wycliffe Global Alliance evelyn_gan@wycliffe.net Start date: FY 2026 End date: FY 2028 Summary Across Southeast Asia, many communities pass along their culture through spoken word—storytelling, song, and drama—rather than through reading and writing. For them, hearing the Bible in these natural forms often connects more deeply than a printed text. Oral Bible Translation is expanding rapidly in Southeast Asia, but the region lacks enough trained people to sustain it. Seminary graduates know the Bible but not oral translation. Practitioners already working need a path to advance their skills. And almost no one is ready to step into consultant roles. Without urgent, structured training, this shortage could stall Oral Bible Translation projects across the region. This three-year project will trains local translators and seminary students in oral Bible translation. Participants move through three stages: a foundation workshop, an advanced workshop and consultant-level training, with only those who show strong skills advancing to the next stage. Our goal is for at least 20 participants, with a smaller group becoming fully qualified to guide future translation projects. Half of the trainers will themselves be new, gaining experience so the program can continue and grow after this project ends. By working in collaboration with Wycliffe Thai Foundation, Wycliffe Malaysia, YWAM Chiang Mai, FCBH, Spoken Worldwide and CRU, the project is rooted in strong partnerships that will ensure sustainability and local ownership. content_zh: 一个为期三年的培训方案将为东南亚各地的当地翻译提供准备,以便将《圣经》变成口头形式,如讲故事和作歌,供通过语音而不是写作分享知识的社区使用。 三个讲习班将培养笔译员的技能,从基本技能到高级技能再到指导技能,因此,至少有20名学员获得当地专门知识。 项目名称:在整个东南亚培训口笔译员 执行组织:怀克里夫全球联盟联系人:伊夫林甘口笔译方案顾问 Wycliffe全球联盟 Eviblyn gan@wycliffe.net 开始日期:2026财政年度 结束日期:东南亚2028财政年度摘要,许多社区通过口语——故事、歌曲和戏剧——而不是通过阅读和写作来传播其文化。 对他们来说,听到这些自然形态的"圣经"往往比印刷文本更深入地连接. 口语圣经翻译在东南亚正在迅速扩张,但该地区缺乏足够的训练有素的人来维持. 修道院毕业生知道"圣经",但不会口头翻译. 已经在工作的从业人员需要一条提高技能的道路。 几乎没有人愿意担任顾问。 如果不进行紧急、有条理的培训,这种短缺可能使整个区域的口语圣经翻译项目陷于停顿。 这个为期三年的项目将对当地翻译和神学院学生进行口语圣经翻译的培训. 与会者分三个阶段:基础讲习班、高级讲习班和顾问一级的培训,只有那些表现出强大技能的人才能进入下一阶段。 我们的目标是至少为20名参与者服务,人数较少的群体将完全有资格指导未来的翻译项目。 一半的训练员会自己是新手,获得经验,以便这个项目结束后方案能够继续并发展. 通过同Wycliffe Thai Foundation、Wycliffe Malaysia、YWAM Chiang Mai、FCBH、Spoken Worldwide和CRU合作,该项目植根于强有力的伙伴关系,将确保可持续性和地方所有权。 给这个工程 点击 现在给到我们的安全赠送门户。 填表时,您将被要求选择一个项目。 在整个东南亚选择培训口笔译员。 所需余额:110 600美元 为了了解更多有关这一资助机会的情况,电子邮件:Evelyn Gan, Wycliffe全球联盟口头翻译方案顾问:evelyn gan@wycliffe.net

title: Training Oral Translators in Indonesia
summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America
summary_zh: 该项目旨在为培训师提供能够在拉丁美洲范围内提供OBT培训的背景知识
title_zh: 在印尼培训口译员
content: Indonesia has hundreds of languages still without Scripture in natural, spoken forms. This three-year program will train 20 local translators and seminary students to fill that gap, building skills from basic to advanced to mentoring. Working with local partners, it aims to grow into a lasting, homegrown training network. Project Name: Training Oral Translators in Indonesia Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance Evelyn Gan Consultant for Oral Translation Programmes Wycliffe Global Alliance evelyn_gan@wycliffe.net Start date: FY 2026 End date: FY 2028 Summary Indonesia is home to hundreds of languages whose speakers pass on knowledge through spoken word rather than writing. Most still lack the Bible in a form that feels natural to hear. Oral Bible Translation is expanding quickly in Indonesia, but training hasn’t kept up—seminary graduates lack oral translation skills, and working practitioners have no path to grow or reach consultant-level readiness. Without urgent, structured training, projects across the country risk stalling. This three-year project trains local translators and seminary students to close that gap. Participants move through three stages—foundational, advanced and consultant-level training—with those who show strong skills advancing to the next stage. Our goal is for at least 20 participants, with a smaller group becoming fully qualified to guide future translation projects on their own. The project partners with several Indonesian organizations, including seminaries, so that this training becomes part of local theological education rather than a one-time effort. That partnership is central to the goal: building lasting, Indonesian-led capacity so that projects no longer depend on outside experts. title: Prayer Wall Guidelines
summary: Questions or comments? Contact us at: Prayer@wycliffe.net
summary_zh: 有问题或意见？联系我们： Prayer@wycliffe.net
title_zh: 祈祷墙指南
content: No login is necessary Please use one of the site languages: English, French, Indonesian, Chinese, Portuguese or Spanish Your item will not appear immediately on the wall. Alliance staff must approve it first. Make sure that you have permission to publish your prayer item . Each item will be available online for anyone to view and will be emailed to subscribers. We do not take responsibility for checking content for security risks. You should have direct permission of any named individual for whom you are asking prayer. If you are naming a language group, please ensure there is no security risk in publishing the name of the language group openly on the internet and in association with a Christian organisation. There is a 280-character limit for each item. At this time you cannot add photos or other attachments to your prayer requests. title: Bible translation’s future is diverse … and local
summary: The ultimate metric of success is no longer just the distribution of physical books, but measurable transformation of lives through deep, culturally authentic understanding.
summary_zh: 衡量成功的最终标准不再仅仅是实体书籍的分发，而是通过深刻的文化真实理解对生活进行可衡量的转变。
title_zh: 圣经翻译的未来是多元化的……和本地
content: Yaoundé, Cameroon — The landscape of global Bible translation is undergoing a paradigm shift, moving away from traditional, agency-led book printing and toward multimodal translations driven by local communities. At a June 2026 gathering in Yaoundé, translation partners and members of Wycliffe Global Alliance organisations spanning Africa, Europe and Latin America reflected on how Scripture is delivered in the 21st century. Their consensus: The ultimate metric of success is no longer just the distribution of physical books, but measurable transformation of lives through deep, culturally authentic understanding. Community-led translation Dr. Paul Kimbi, the Alliance’s Consultant for Bible Translation Programmes, said Bible translation’s future belongs to community dialogue rather than isolated translation agencies. This emerging approach, known as conversational translation, prioritises localised, grassroots work: listening intimately to communities, engaging them in active storytelling and using locally adapted communication channels. As multiple translation agencies increasingly operate within the same borders, global leaders are urging a shift toward radical collaboration. ‘The multiplicity of agencies is not a hindrance; however, harmony and unity are essential,’ Kimbi said. ‘Unity does not mean uniformity. Each agency, according to its unique strengths, approaches Bible translation as a collaborative piece of God’s global mission.’ Multimodal translations will better serve people from different contexts . Beyond the Book: Multimodal and AI Integration Because cultural contexts vary wildly across the globe, the Alliance’s Africa Area gathering highlighted the urgent need for ‘embodied and multimodal’ translations. This means managing multiple streams of communication simultaneously—integrating oral storytelling, vibrant illustrations, written text and digital media. ‘We do not communicate only with words; we communicate with colours, images, and multimedia,’ Kimbi said. ‘We can no longer consider translation strictly as a written book, but rather as a dynamic multimodal experience.’ This digital evolution naturally intersects with the rise of artificial intelligence. While delegates recognised AI’s immense potential to increase translation speed, optimise efficiency and lower operational costs for minority languages, attendees maintained a stance of strategic caution. ‘Technology accelerates the advancement of Bible translation and language development, but it also creates new strategic responsibilities for leaders and organisations,’ said Etienne Ondoa, a language technology consultant. Staff capacity building, therefore, remains the greatest investment, he said. As technology evolves, the skills required to support it in ministry also evolve. ‘Technological leadership should have a voice in strategic decision-making processes, Ondoa said. ‘Technological decisions increasingly influence ministry outcomes, sound financial resource management, cybersecurity, AI adoption and organisational resilience.’ Etienne Ondoa A Symphony for the Global Church Ultimately, leaders at the event reaffirmed that translation organisations do not operate in a vacuum. They exist to serve the church, which remains God’s primary vehicle for global mission. Kimbi likened the future of the movement to a grand, global arrangement. ‘The particularity of modern Bible translation is that it is a diverse ensemble—an orchestra of varied influences interpreting a magnificent symphony titled ‘Scriptures’ for every language community,’ he said. ‘And in this orchestra, we need everyone: local churches, oral communicators, media creators, literacy specialists and technology partners.’ Story: Lune Prudence Mvondo and Isaac Forchie Photos: Isaac Forchie
content_zh: 喀麦隆雅温得 全球圣经翻译的地貌正在发生范式转变,从传统的、机构主导的书籍印刷转向由当地社区驱动的多模式翻译。 在2026年6月的雅温得集会上,翻译伙伴和遍布非洲、欧洲和拉丁美洲的维克利夫全球联盟组织的成员反思了21世纪如何交付《圣经》。 他们的共识: 衡量成功与否的终极尺度不再仅仅是物理图书的发行,而是通过深刻,文化上真实的理解,对生活进行可测量的转变. 联盟的圣经翻译方案顾问Paul Kimbi博士说,圣经翻译的未来属于社区对话而不是孤立的翻译机构。 这种新兴方法被称为对话翻译、地方化优先化、基层工作:密切听取社区的意见,让他们参与积极讲故事,并使用适合当地情况的交流渠道。 随着多个翻译机构越来越多地在同一边界内运作,全球领导人正在敦促向根本合作转变。 Kimbi说 : “ 机构繁多并非障碍, `团结并不意味着统一。 每个机构都根据其独特的长处,将圣经翻译视为上帝全球使命的合作作品。 多式联运将更好地为来自不同背景的人服务。 除了《书:多式联运和人工智能一体化》之外,由于世界各地的文化背景大相径庭,联盟的非洲地区会议强调迫切需要 " 健全和多模式 " 翻译。 这意味着同时管理多种通信流——将口头讲故事、活泼的插图、书面文字和数字媒体结合起来。 Kimbi说 : “ 我们不只用文字沟通, 我们不能再严格地认为翻译是一本书, 这种数字演变自然地与人工智能的兴起相交. 虽然代表们承认大赦国际在提高翻译速度、优化效率和降低少数民族语言的业务费用方面具有巨大潜力,但与会者保持战略谨慎的立场。 语言技术顾问Etienne Ondoa说, “技术加速了圣经翻译和语言发展的进步, 因此,他说,工作人员的能力建设仍然是最大的投资。 随着技术的发展,部内支持技术所需的技能也随之而来. Ondoa说,“技术领导在战略决策进程中应有发言权。 “技术决定日益影响部委的成果、健全的财政资源管理、网络安全、人工智能的采用和组织复原力。” Etienne Ondoa是全球教会的交响乐团, 它们的存在是为了为教会服务,而教会仍然是上帝执行全球任务的主要工具。 金比把运动的未来比作一个宏伟的全球安排. 他说,“现代圣经译本的特殊性在于它是一个多样化的合唱团——由各种影响组成的管弦乐团,为每个语言群体解释一首名为 " 脚本 " 的宏伟交响乐。 “在这个管弦乐团中,我们需要每个人:地方教会、口头宣传者、媒体创造者、扫盲专家和技术伙伴。” 故事:吕恩·普鲁登斯·姆冯多和艾萨克·福奇相片:艾萨克·福奇相片

content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. So this has become my nod to the need for daily exercise. Being one of the few beings on the planet who still buys a hard copy of a daily newspaper, I take my hound – a cocker spaniel with unusually short legs – with me of a morning. content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get

title_zh: 如果你的教会唱希尔松歌，而你希望它不会唱，该怎么办？
content: A few weeks ago, I explained why my church does not sing songs by Hillsong , and, by the same convictions, songs by Bethel and Elevation. I tried to be clear that I do not understand this to be a matter of clear right or wrong, but rather a matter of wisdom and conscience. While this is a decision we have made for our church, I would not look down on churches that choose differently. I wish I had addressed a related matter at that time: what should you do if you see this issue in the way I do, but the leaders of your church do not? In other words, what should you do if your church sings Hillsong, but you wish it wouldn’t? I want to offer just a few thoughts on that. In general, I would suggest you just sing the songs, provided they do not require you to sing anything that is unbiblical. And thankfully, the majority of the songs by Hillsong, Bethel, and Elevation will not force you to sing error. That said, there are a few songs that may come close, or whose lyrics are imprecise enough that they could be understood in different ways. For example, Hillsong’s “So Will I (100 Billion X)” has these words in its second verse and the chorus that follows it: All nature and science Follow the sound of Your voice And as you speak A hundred billion creatures catch your breath Evolving in pursuit of what you said If it all reveals your nature so will I The most natural reading of those words is an affirmation of some kind of theistic evolution. I could not sing that, and I understand that you may not be able to either. Bethel’s “Reckless Love” continually ascribes recklessness to God. Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God Oh, it chases me down, fights ’til I’m found, leaves the ninety-nine I couldn’t earn it, I don’t deserve it, still You give Yourself away Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God It is difficult for me ( and for John Piper , as it happens) to find a sense in which the word “reckless” is a fitting word for God. I think I know what the songwriters were hoping to convey with the word, but “reckless” is not suitable when speaking of God’s love and purposes, and I understand why many Christians could simply not permit themselves to sing it. I couldn’t either. But apart from those songs and a few others, most do not contain lyrics that are false or wrong. If your elders have deemed these songs suitable for your church, then it’s probably best to sing them in submission to the people whose leadership you have decided to follow. There is no “followership” in this world, other than following Christ, that does not at times involve submitting our own preferences to the preferences of our leaders. It would probably be a good time for a reminder that you just can’t have it all on this side of glory. Every pastor, every eldership, and every church will have both strengths and weaknesses. Too many Christians (who are also a bewildering collection of both strengths and weaknesses, of course) spend their whole lives searching for a perfect church, never quite grasping that it’s a futile effort. They go to the church with great preaching, but find that its evangelism is disappointing; they head for the church with great evangelism, but find its polity is poor. They soon switch again, this time choosing the church with their preferred polity, only to discover that it’s lacking in fellowship. They never learn the joy of settling into an imperfect church, in which they can rejoice in the strengths while bearing with the weaknesses. Sometimes accepting those weaknesses means singing songs or tolerating musical styles that are not aligned with their preferences, even when that’s hard to do. But what if the church does sing those songs that have actual errors in them? In the moment, I’d suggest you simply stop singing and refrain from making a big deal of it. You don’t need to make a fuss or storm out. But afterward, it would be wise to speak with your pastors to address your concerns, humbly, of course, and w

几周前,我解释了为什么我的教堂 不唱山歌, 和同样的信念, 由贝瑟尔和Elevation的歌曲。 我试图表明,我不理解这是一个明确对错的问题,而是一个智慧和良心的问题。 虽然这是我们为我们的教会所做的决定,但我不会轻视那些选择不同的教会.

我希望当时我已谈到一个相关的问题:如果你以我的方式看待这个问题,但你们教会的领导人却不这样做,那你们应该怎么做? 换句话说,如果你的教堂唱山歌, 我只想就此提出几点想法。

一般来说,我建议你只是唱 歌曲,只要它们不要求你 唱任何非圣经。 谢天谢地,希尔松,贝瑟尔和Elevation的歌曲大多不会强迫你唱出错误. 虽然如此,也有几首歌可能接近,或者歌词不够精确,以至于可以以不同的方式被理解.

例如,Hillsong的"So Will I (1000亿 X)"的第二首诗中有这些词,下面的合唱: 所有自然和科学都跟着你的声音 当你说话时,一千亿生物 抓住你的呼吸 进取地追求你说的 如果这一切揭示你的本性,我也会 这些话最自然的读取是肯定某种神论

ution. 我无法唱出这首歌 我理解你也可能无法唱出这首歌 贝瑟尔的"无颈之爱"不断将鲁莽归咎于上帝.

我无法挣取的九十九分钱, 我并不配得到, 你还是放弃你自己。 我很难找到一种感觉,即“无畏”一词对上帝来说是合适的。

我想我知道那些作曲者希望用这个词表达什么,但是在谈论上帝的爱和宗旨时,“无畏”并不合适,我理解为什么许多基督徒不能允许自己唱出它。 我也不能。 但除这些歌曲和少数其他歌曲外,大多数歌曲没有包含虚假或错误的歌词.

如果你的长辈认为这首歌适合你的教会, 那么, 这个世界除了追随基督之外,没有“追随者”有时并不涉及我们自己对我们领导人的偏好。

可能是时候提醒大家, 每个牧师,每个长老,每个教会都会有优缺点. 太多的基督徒(当然,他们也是充满了优缺点和优缺点的令人困惑的集合者)毕生都在寻找一个完美的教堂,从不完全理解这是一个徒劳的努力。

他们带着伟大的传道去教堂,但发现其福音派令人失望;他们带着伟大的福音派去教堂,但发现其政体贫乏. 他们很快又转了身, 这次是用他们喜欢的政体选择教会,

他们永远无法学会安顿在一个不完善的教堂中的欢乐,在教堂里,他们可以在承受弱点的同时为长处而欢喜. 有时接受这些弱点意味着唱出歌曲或容忍不符合其喜好的音乐风格,即使这很难做到。 但是如果教会确实唱了那些有实际错误的歌呢?

我建议你别再唱歌, 你不需要大惊小怪, 但事后,明智的做法是与你的牧师们交谈 解决你的顾虑,当然,谦卑,和W

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several excellent biographies from Crossway. Each of them is good, but I’m partial to the one on R.C. Sproul. Note that these biographies are typically priced between $22 and $40. In case you missed it on the weekend, Westminster Books is offering a deep discount on the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . Recommended Reading Christianity Under the Progressive Gaze. Kyle Borg: “What interests me more than politics is the apparent cultural strength and growing respectability of progressive Christianity. In fact, a headline in The Guardian boldly declared: ‘A progressive understanding of Christianity won in the US elections.’ In a society where historic Christian convictions — and I don’t just mean Reformed confessionalism but basic creedal Christianity — is often treated with suspicion, if not hostility, some expressions of ‘Christianity’ seem to be enjoying a rather warm reception.” Counterfeit Providence: Why Christians Must Reject the Conspiratorial Mind. Mitchell Bahnsen explores the conspiratorial mind and explains why it’s so important for Christians to reject it. “None of this requires Christians to become gullible or naive. Psalm 2 describes kings taking counsel together against the Lord, and the crucifixion itself was a conspiracy carried out jointly by religious and governmental authorities. True connivance does occur, and wisdom to discern the truth is necessary in a complex and fallen world. However, we must defend against a totalizing hermeneutic of suspicion, lest it become its own form of faith.” Wise People Strive To Be Wiser. Justin Huffman discusses a principle that may be obvious, but is also important. “The wise person is always seeking to become wiser still. The truly spiritual person recognizes his or her constant need for spiritual growth.” The Pro-Life Movement’s Midterm Reckoning. First Things allows everyone to access several free articles per month, and this one from Jonathon Van Maren is worth one of the quota. He considers how the battle against abortion is likely to look very different after the midterm elections. “‘It’s impossible to sugarcoat it,’ Marjorie Dannenfelser of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America wrote in a memo issued on November 3. The 2026 midterm election results ‘are a disaster for the unborn, for their mothers, and for the country as a whole. Democrats are on track to control two of the three pieces they need to legalize taxpayer-funded abortion on demand, up until birth, in all fifty states—something they promise to start pushing as soon as they take office in January.'” How Evil Works. John Piper helpfully explains how evil works. “At the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfully accuse you of unforgiven sin in heaven, you will perish. And Jesus calls him ‘a murderer from the beginning’ (John 8:44). So, the deception and the accusation and the eternal death that results from unforgiven sin is a way of destroying people and opposing God.” Preaching in Paragraphs. This may be helpful for preachers to read as they let last week’s sermon fade into the past and begin to think about the next one. “Every preacher knows the terror of a blank screen. It is Tuesday morning—or even worse, Saturday afternoon—and the preacher sits and stares at his laptop. He has opened a new document in his word processor, and now the cursor stands idling on the page, patiently blinking. And the words aren’t coming.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re reading this via email, you’ll need to visit my site to fill out the form. Go here to read last week’s recommendations.) Submit

content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: His Will Will Be Done Photomicrography Come, Thou Fount (×3) The Brain-Injured Musical Genius Grain from an Attic Prepare Him Room (Live) 1. His Will Will Be Done To have power is to have ability and strength. This is true whether the power belongs to human beings or to God himself—to creatures or to the Creator. Of course, our power is derived from God’s, but his is inherent. We are accountable to God for the way we use our power, but God is accountable only to himself. Our power is always small and incomplete, but God’s is always unbounded and unlimited. To say we are powerful is to say we possess the ability to do some of the things we desire some of the time. But to say God is powerful is to say God always possesses within himself the means necessary to bring about whatsoever he wills—to execute all his plans, to execute them all the way to perfect completion, and to overcome any and all resistance. This guarantees that God’s will will be done, for as the psalmist says, “Our God is in the heavens; he does all that he pleases” (Psalm 115:3). The God we worship today is the God for whom this is true: Whatever his will resolves and however his wisdom directs, his power will accomplish. 2. Photomicrography Shall we look at the results of another photography competition? Why yes, we shall. This week it’s Nikon’s Photomicrography Competition . “What is photomicrography you ask” (other than a word that is almost impossible to type correctly the first time, or even the fourth, in my case)? It is taking photos of microscopic objects and, in that way, opening a view to a world that is otherwise far too small for us to see. I think you’ll enjoy browsing the winners, which include spiders, pens, neurons, and inkjet printers. 3. Come, Thou Fount (×3) I really enjoy The National Parks and their delightful, easy-to-listen-to folk-Americana music. It’s my understanding that they grew up Mormon but have spoken openly about leaving that faith, but I am not aware of them becoming Christian. I was surprised, then, to see they had released a version of “ Come, Thou Fount .” It’s quite a good one. I’m not sure what motivated them to record it, but perhaps it was the same thing that motivated Marcus Mumford of Mumford & Sons, who has also recorded and performed it several times—I assume it was just the sheer beauty of the song. Mumford was raised in a Christian home, though later left the faith. His version is also wonderful. Another favorite rendition, sung by Christians, is this one by Celtic Worship . 4. The Brain-Injured Musical Genius The New York Times had an amazing feature this week, and it was amazing in two ways. First, it was beautifully put together with animated graphics and other visual elements. Second, it told a remarkable story—the story of a man who suffered a terrible brain injury but, through it, became a musical genius. I think you’ll enjoy reading The Brain Injury That Made a Middle School Teacher a Musical Genius . 5. Grain from an Attic Here’s a fun story from Italy that pastors may want to hang on to for future sermon illustrations. In the early 1990s, a farmer in Parma found some old seeds in his attic. He assumed they were useless, so he tossed them on the manure pile. Much to his surprise, they sprouted into a form of grain he had never seen before. I’ll leave you to read the story, look at the pictures, and consider the many possible illustrations and applications. Photo credit: Clara Vannucci 6. Prepare Him Room (Live) A couple of days ago, a friend told me that his children had begun listening to Christmas music, and we discussed whether it’s still too early in the year for that. We agreed that you don’t want to begin listening too early lest you grow tired of the relatively limited catalog of songs before Christma

title_zh: 周末单点菜肴（ 11月7日）
content: Welcome to Weekend A La Carte. I hope you find something here, whether a longform article, a reader recommendation, or something else entirely, that makes your weekend just a little bit better. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several newer and older books that are all worth at least thinking about. If you’re interested in doing some theological reading, Westminster Books is offering up to 57% off the three-volume set of Warfield’s works. Also, I haven’t reviewed it yet, but did want to briefly recommend the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . It seems to be priced just about equally at Westminster Books and Amazon (for me, at least). Recommended Reading Canada’s Maclean’s magazine has an interesting article about the Hutterites and their caution when it comes to modern technologies. The author, like so many of us, is alarmed by the ways technology overtakes our lives, and sees that the Hutterites may have a healthier relationship to it. Most of us—including me—are worried that we’ve all become desensitized to the manifold and multiplying ways technology is negatively affecting our lives. Social media has been blamed for rising rates of political polarization and radicalization, damaging young people’s ability to form relationships and eroding mental health. And we’re all trying to figure out what to do about it. Slick startups sell devices you tap with your phone to “brick” it (that is, blocking distracting social media, apps and internet access). There are apps to remove short-form videos from social media feeds. There are now social media bans in place for youth in Australia, in parts of Europe and Asia and, this June, proposed in Canada. Sales of dumbphones and flip phones have grown in the past few years. Even landlines are trendy again. But this is like pushing back the tide with a broom. For most of us, technology feels like a force of nature that will wash over us whether we want it to or not. The Hutterites are more optimistic. They think if they can keep their distance from the wider world, and adopt the right set of rules around technology, they can hold onto its positive features and simply seal out what they don’t like. Read: The Hutterites’ Guide to Technology. The New York Times was in touch with many Gen Zers and explains how their entry into the job market is much different from previous generations. I think it’s easy for those of us who are older to act as if Gen Z is lazy or otherwise not putting in much effort, but this article ought to give us some compassion. They described a process that is lonely, opaque and impersonal, in which it is hard to tell whether one is being rejected by a hiring manager or an A.I. screener. The problem is not just that hiring has slowed across the labor market, or that the specter of A.I. is threatening entry-level positions, they said. It was that they could not get a real, live human being to speak to them. Ever. About anything. The same language came up over and over in their responses: They felt as if they were throwing their applications into “the void.” Some of them opted for slightly different terminology — a “black hole” or an “abyss” — but they painted a similar picture of the application process as a swirling vortex where aspirations and cover letters vanish, unlikely to be retrieved. One part that jumped out to me was the person who insists on they/them pronouns. I would imagine that is a huge red flag for people in charge of hiring! Read: Searching for Jobs, Gen Z Feels Like It’s Staring Into ‘The Void’. The Verge has a lengthy article that describes the bizarre and heterodox gospel according to Peter Thiel. It’s a time of apocalyptic worldviews in Silicon Valley. The latest AI doom cycle is driven by effective altruism (EA), a philosophy that has lurked around the fringes for years but recently burst into the mainstream because its adherents are embedded across the AI industry, from Anthropic to newly appointed AI safety watchdog METR. summary: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. summary_zh: 亲爱的读者，很遗憾地通知您，天堂旅游又回来了。这种风格可能永远不会完全消失，但它至少在畅销书榜上消失了好几年。可悲的是，它在加布·波洛的《天堂18天》中又回来了。另请参阅我对畅销书的热门书评：天堂是真正的来自天堂的问候：天堂旅游的现代历史
title_zh: 很遗憾地通知您，天堂旅游又回来了
content: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven , which was one of the bestselling Christian books last month and even made its way to the New York Times list of bestsellers—a feat most authors can only dream of. Out of sheer magnanimity (and perhaps a morbid sense of curiosity), I read it so you don’t have to. 18 Days in Heaven Gabe Poirot Before I tell you what it’s all about, here’s a brief history of heaven tourism. Don Piper kicked off the genre in 2004 with 90 Minutes in Heaven , and it proved a surprise hit that quickly dominated the sales charts, eventually tallying upwards of 8 million copies sold. Todd Burpo’s Heaven Is for Real followed in 2010 with over 10 million copies sold. That same year brought Kevin and Alex Malarkey’s The Boy Who Came Back from Heaven , which sold more than a million copies before Alex recanted his story and the publisher pulled it. The genre went on to deliver many more heaven books and a handful of less-popular hell books like Bill Wiese’s 23 Minutes in Hell , though none ever reached the same heights as the first few—no pun intended. My contribution to the genre was little more than reviewing several of the books and coining the snarky phrase “heaven tourism,” which, much to my delight, soon caught on . The genre inevitably ran its course, but has now returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven: I Left My Body. I Met Jesus. What He Told Me Will Alter Your Eternity . Sadly, but not surprisingly, it is just as bad as its predecessors, mixing truth with errors and documented facts with spurious speculations until it is as confusing and unreliable as any of them. 18 Days in Heaven follows the standard pattern by beginning with an account of a terrible accident—in this case, a head injury that resulted from a skateboarding mishap. Poirot, a young evangelist with a sizable YouTube following, was rendered comatose and remained hovering between life and death for 18 days. But while his body was inert, his soul was transported to heaven, where it experienced heavenly wonders, not the least of which was spending time with Jesus. What did he see and experience there? Many things, of course, some of which he is able to describe and many of which he insists he cannot, either because God told him not to or because they defy description. What can he describe? Jesus’s eyes, in which “I saw all the colors that had ever existed or could exist, all in one. He was the deepest ocean of liquid love that had no end. A spectrum of intensity that only increased the longer I stared. His eyebrows, hair, jawline, arms, chest, heart, stature, ears, forehead, eyelashes, teeth, mouth, skin, and complexion all said the same thing: I love you, I love you, I love you.” He describes Jesus’s scars which “were like an ocean that had no floor,” and had the name “Gabriel” written immediately above them. He learned from them that Jesus has completely and eternally forgotten his sins so that he could no longer remember them even if he wanted to. He smelled Jesus and observed that his “fragrance wasn’t like the humidity of the Florida Everglades. No, this was something eternal—an everlasting fountain of fire, not just surrounding me but burning into me. Wrapping around me like a robe, like a living garment of pure, unending presence. It felt burning hot and freezing cold at the same time.” He heard Jesus say many words and noted that his “words were not just a separate entity that He ‘released.’ They were like the sharpest spears that went right into the core of my very being. But these spears were not separate from Him—they were Him.” Poirot even saw his own conception: “The light from Father God united with the earthly seed from my father and the egg of my mother in that moment, and I began my existence on earth. I was not born just on

我对这个流派的贡献不过是回顾几本书, 但现在又回到了Gabe Poirot在天堂的18天:我离开了我的身体。 我遇见了耶稣。 他告诉我 Will 改变你的永恒

可悲但并不令人惊讶的是,它同其前身一样糟糕,把事实与错误相混淆,把有记录的事实同虚假的猜测相混淆,直到它同其中任何一个都一样令人困惑和不可靠。 18天的"天堂"遵循了标准模式,首先讲述了一起可怕的事故——在此情况下,由于滑板出事而造成头部受伤.

Poirot是一位年轻的福音传播者,他带着一个庞大的YouTube跟随,因此被昏迷并徘徊在生与死之间长达18天. 但虽然他的身体是惰性的,他的灵魂被运到了天堂,在那里它经历了天堂的奇事,其中最起碼是和耶稣一起度过. 他在那里看到了什么? 体验什么?

当然,许多事情,有些是他能够描述的,有些是他坚持不能描述的,要么是因为上帝告诉他不要描述,要么是因为他们藐视描述。 他能描述什么? 耶稣的眼睛,其中,“我看到了曾经存在或可能存在的所有颜色,都是一种颜色。 他是无尽的液体爱最深的海洋

强度的光谱 只会增加我恒星的长度 他的眉毛、发型、下巴、手臂、胸部、心、身高、耳朵、额头、睫毛、牙齿、口腔、皮肤和相貌都说了同样的话:我爱你,我爱你,我爱你。” 他描述了耶稣的伤疤,这些伤疤 " 像一片没有地的海洋 " ,上面写有 " Gabriel " 的名字。

他从他们那里得知,耶稣已经彻底地,永远地忘记了自己的罪过,这样即使他愿意也再也记不住了. 他闻到耶稣的气味并观察到他的"香气不像佛罗里达埃弗格拉德河的湿润. 不,这是永恒的东西, 一个永恒的火焰喷泉, 不仅包围着我,而且燃烧在我身上。

缠绕我就像长袍一样 像纯洁无尽的活衣 它同时感到被烧得发热而冷冻。” 他听到耶稣说出许多话,并指出他的"词不仅是一个他‘释放'的独立实体. 他们就像最锋利的长矛 直入我生命的核心

这些长矛,不是与他分开的,他们确是他。 波洛甚至看到了自己的构想:“神父所赐的光与我父亲所赐的地上种子和母亲的卵合而为一,我开始了我在地上的存在。 我不是刚出生

content: Good morning. I’ve got A La Carte and a regretful book review for you today. Over the weekend you’ll find Saturday’s Weekend A La Carte plus Sunday’s Works & Wonders, which shares content that is just right for a Sunday morning. I hope you enjoy reading it all as much as I have enjoyed putting it together. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals are headlined by Joel Beeke’s A Radical, Comprehensive Call to Holiness . You may also be interested in a book about women who overcame a difficult past or a biography written for a younger audience. Recommended Reading Selfies Are Not the Self: Forming Embodied Youth in a Disembodied Age. This article from Harvest USA has some helpful insights about young people and their mobile devices. “Increasingly, research shows that teenagers know their technology is making them miserable. They don’t love their phones, but they hate missing out. They know the noise is making them sick, but they’re terrified of the silence. When teenagers are so thirsty for connection and validation that they’ll go to a well they know is poisoned just to get a drink, what an amazing opportunity we have as the church to offer something better, something truly beautiful. We don’t want our youth ministries to be known for what they lack. We want them to be known for their abundance.” Can’t You Just Love Everyone? Jeremy Walker addresses churches that think their calling is to “just love everyone.” “Why not just love one another? Why build walls, make distinctions, establish boundaries, and draw lines? Why confront sins? Why not welcome all equally? Can’t you just love everyone?” 4 Applications for the Order of Love—From the Home to the Ends of the Earth. Speaking of love, Alex Kocman addresses the necessity of rightly ordering our love. “Augustine’s idea of ordo amoris —the ‘order of love’—reflects the Scriptural pattern of directing our affections to first love God, then to love our families, and then to extend that love outward to others. This theme of ordered love has wide-ranging implications—from the home to the ends of the earth. But just as preaching without application is lifeless, so too is a study of love without practical exhortation. Here are four admonitions…” Effective Altruists and the Spreadsheet Gospel. Writing for TGC, Nathan Leamer addresses the effective altruism ideology that is so influential in Silicon Valley. “Over the past decade, an emergent secular philosophy has taken root in Silicon Valley. It now drives many conversations around politics and technology, particularly as its ideas shape how our society approaches artificial intelligence. Known as ‘effective altruism,’ this worldview is having a moment. The Economist recently called the philosophy ‘this century’s biggest idea’ and labeled the movement as ‘admirable, but dangerous.'” Your Thoughts Are Shaping Your Life. “Your thoughts are shaping your life.” That might sound like the kind of thing Joel Osteen or a New Age practitioner would say, but there is truth to it. “Our thought life matters more than we often realize. The conversations we replay in our minds, the offenses we revisit, and the fears we entertain can shape how we see our circumstances and respond to the people around us. I know how easily my thoughts can become consumed by something that has happened or something I fear might happen. Before long, I find myself responding to the present through the lens of thoughts I have been rehearsing.” Don’t Despise the Red Flags. Katie Laitkep writes to those who are dating, and to young women specifically, to warn them not to ignore or despise the red flags. “When we see signs marking a dangerous road, we respond immediately, knowing we need to find a different path. But when it comes to red flags in dating relationships, we don’t always view the warning signs as clearly.” Reviews I like to share the occasional reminder that it is tremendously helpful to authors if you post even brief reviews of their books at Amazon. content: May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a couple of Christmas devotionals, a Greg Koukl classic, and Seth Lewis’s Dream Small , among others. In case it’s of interest, Audible continues to offer a great deal—three months of service plus a $20 bonus for $0.99/month. You can unsubscribe at any time. Recommended Reading A Manifesto for Phone-Free Church. This article offers a lot to think about when it comes to the consequences of using our phones in church. “Distractions in worship will be with us always, but that does not mean we ought to go out into the highways and the hedges and invite as many distractions as possible. And here, we should note that there are good distractions in church—I am thinking of those babies that cry and fuss and laugh at all the wrong moments. Good distractions remind us that church is more than our personal ‘alone time’ with God. We are part of a family.” The Missing Piece in John Mark Comer’s Quiet Time. I think Matthew Bingham’s review of John Mark Comer’s book is bang on in both what it praises and what it criticizes. “Though Comer identifies as a Protestant, he relies on numerous quotations from ‘desert fathers and mothers,’ medieval mystics, and modern Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox theologians to justify his cafeteria approach to spirituality. As in his previous work, he engages with few heirs of the Reformation. Comer insists that Scripture is essential, but, for him, it doesn’t stand alone. Consistent with this non-Protestant mystical tradition, the book strongly emphasizes subjective, immediate communication from God apart from God’s inspired words in Scripture.” Free Chick-fil-A For a Year. Did you know that Midwestern Seminary is home to Spurgeon College, which is an undergraduate school that exists to equip students for the Kingdom? This November, they’re giving away a year’s supply of Chick-fil-A! Head over here to enter to win and discover other opportunities to grow deeper in Christ this month! (Sponsored) The Pull of Rome and the Promise of Grace. Chris Castaldo writes about those who are drawn to Rome. “A member of your small group confesses, seemingly out of the blue, that he’s been attending Mass. Next, you hear a deacon wonder aloud if we really needed to break with Rome. Then a family member announces that she has ‘crossed the Tiber,’ meaning she has converted to Roman Catholicism. Such conversations seem to be happening with greater frequency in Protestant circles. But why?” 4 Misconceptions About Spiritual Warfare. Costi Hinn outlines four fairly common misconceptions about spiritual warfare. “There is a short list of Christian beliefs that have as much mystery as spiritual warfare. While some things are really clear in the Bible regarding demons and demonic activity, there is a supernatural element to the unseen realm that humbles even the most educated theological student! At the same time, it seems that many people have a variety of opinions based on their experiences, which is not necessarily a negative thing, but it can lead to a lot of misconceptions.” Slouching Toward Narnia. Personally I’ve been enjoying reading all the different perspectives on the growing information we have about the forthcoming Narnia film(s). I think Nicholas McDonald’s article is one of the best so far. He explains his formula for a successful film adaptation (Faithfulness to Theme + Thoughtful Innovations = Great Film Adaptation) and tells whether he’s feeling hopeful as he considers The Magician’s Nephew in that way. Four Corrections to Make When You Feel Guilty About Your Giving. I think most people feel guilty about their giving from time to time. When that’s true of you, here are some ways you can correct the way you think and act. 同时,看来许多人根据自己的经历有各种观点,这不一定是负面的东西,但会导致许多误解". 向纳尼亚走去 我个人一直喜欢阅读关于纳尼亚电影的不断增长的信息,

title: A Daring Suggestion for Netflix
summary: Netflix appears to have fallen on hard times and I have some suggestions that I'd like to think would help it: cut the sex, nudity, and profanity, and gain back the viewers it's long been alienating. See Also A La Carte (April 28) A La Carte (October 22) Netflix’s Biggest Competition
summary_zh: Netflix似乎陷入了困境，我提出了一些我认为会有所帮助的建议：减少性、裸露和亵渎，并赢回长期以来一直疏远的观众。另请参阅点菜（ 4月28日）点菜（ 10月22日） Netflix最大的比赛
title_zh: 对Netflix的大胆建议
content: Netflix appears to have fallen on hard times. The company’s co-CEOs recently announced they would be laying off around 1,000 employees, the deepest round of cuts in years. A day later, the chief content officer made a sudden exit and was immediately replaced. Just a week after that, the market responded unfavorably to Netflix’s Q3 results, causing the stock to drop sharply. There are many reasons for Netflix’s woes, not the least of which are increasingly heavy competition for viewers and its failure to land marquee shows—the kind of shows that convince people to maintain their subscription instead of canceling it in favor of Disney+, Prime Video, or one of the many other options. While there’s little doubt that Netflix will make it through this challenge, it may never regain the market dominance it once held. I have a daring suggestion for Netflix that I’d like to think could help it: make more shows that are clean and suitable for family viewing. To frame it another way, stop putting sex, nudity, and harsh profanity in nearly every show. There are many potential subscribers who are eager to be entertained, but not by shows they deem unsuitable or inappropriate. I’ll grant that Netflix has viewing data that probably shows its TV-MA content is especially popular, but data can only count the people who watched a show, not the ones who never pressed play in the first place. It’s also can’t tell whether the sex and swearing are essential to those who watch it, or whether they’d watch it even if it was much cleaner. Perhaps you could think about it this way: a single explicit sex scene in a series is unlikely to gain more viewers than it will lose. What I mean is that a content warning on IMDb or Common Sense Media stating that a show contains an explicit sex scene is enough for me and many others to skip that entire show. But I very much doubt the opposite is true—that a person will learn that there is no sex scene and decide to skip it on that basis. Some of us simply have no interest in viewing such things and will guard both ourselves and our families from seeing them. For those who don’t believe me, I’m sure I can put them in touch with a thousand people who will affirm what I’m saying. I am convinced there is a deep desire for shows and movies we can watch without cringing, without feeling violated, and without knowing we are watching what we consider not only unsuitable but immoral. It’s not that we’re prudes or opposed to sex—we’re all for it. It’s that we think sex and nudity are for private contexts , not public ones, and that some matters are to be kept between a husband and wife rather than displayed for all the world to see. Sex is so good and powerful that making it public diminishes it rather than elevates it, which means we deliberately avoid shows and movies that feature it. I would say something similar about language . Does a show need to drop hundreds of F-bombs across just a few hours of runtime? Does it need to constantly use the name of God as a swear word? It doesn’t need any of this. Once again, is it more likely that people will not watch shows unless they are profane, or that they will avoid them if they are? I think the answer is obvious: many more people will be driven away by swearing than drawn by it. If I had to offer one more piece of advice, it would be to stop tampering with beloved intellectual properties to make them consistent with modern sensibilities. Why not just make adaptations that are faithful to the vision of the original creators and let us deal with the differences between their context and today’s? Have the courage to let the stories stand on their own without inserting modern messaging. I strongly believe this would do more to provoke good thinking and spur important conversations. There’s no need to be so heavy-handed. To summarize, I think Netflix has been going about this all wrong and has been creating content that alienates an eager audience rather than drawing it in.
