content_zh:
Netflix似乎陷入了困难时期. 公司联合首席执行官最近宣布将解雇约1000名员工,这是多年来最大幅度的削减。 一天后,首席内容官突然退出,立即被替换. 仅仅一周后,市场对Netflix的Q3结果反应不佳,导致股票急剧下降.

Netflix的悲哀有许多原因, 更是观众竞争日益激烈, 以及它未能登陆马奎节目,

Netflix虽然毫无疑问会渡过这个挑战,但可能永远无法恢复它曾经占据的市场支配地位。 我对Netflix有一个大胆的建议, 我想可以帮助它: 做更多干净、适合家庭观看的节目。 以另一种方式设定它,停止把性,裸体,以及苛刻的淫秽在几乎所有的节目中.

有许多潜在的订阅者渴望娱乐,但并不是通过他们认为不合适或不适当的展示。 我同意Netflix的收看数据可能显示其TV-MA内容特别受欢迎,

也无法分辨性与誓词对于观看者是否至关重要, 也许你可以这样想: 系列中一个单一的显性场景不太可能获得比它失去的更多的观众.

我的意思是,一个内容警告 互联网电影数据库(IMDb)上或Common Sense Media上 声明,一个节目包含一个明确的性场景,足够我和许多其他人跳过整个节目. 但我非常怀疑相反的情况是真实的——一个人会得知没有性场景,并据此决定跳过.

我们中有些人根本不关心看这些东西,并将保护我们自己和我们的家人不看到它们。 我敢肯定, 我可以和一千人联系,

我深信,人们非常渴望看一些节目和电影,而无需相信,无需感到被侵犯,也无需知道我们正在看我们认为不合适和不道德的东西。 我们不是故意或反对性爱,

我们觉得性与裸体是私人事务, 性是如此的美好和强大, 使它公开 减少它而不是提升它, 这意味着我们故意避免 节目和电影 我会说类似的东西的语言。

演出需要投下数百枚F炸弹吗? 难道它需要不断使用上帝之名作为誓词吗? 它不需要这些。 复次,是人不看秀,非有妄言,或避之不见,更何况?

我认为答案是显而易见的:更多的人会因为宣誓而被驱逐,而不是被它吸引。 如果我不得不再提一个建议,那就是停止篡改所爱的知识产权,使之符合现代的敏感性.

为何不只做忠实于原始创造者愿景的改编,让我们处理他们的背景与今天的不同? 要有勇气让这些故事独立存在,而不插入现代信息。 我坚信,这将更有助于激发良好的思维,刺激重要的对话。 也不必如此粗暴。

总结一下,我认为Netflix一直把事情搞错了,并创造出让热心的观众疏远的内容,而不是把它引进来. 所以说网友

content: Good morning. The God of peace be with you today. Sales & Deals Some of today’s noteworthy Kindle deals include Al Mohler’s reader-friendly commentary on Hebrews, Julie Lowe’s guide to safeguarding our homes, and Marty Machowski’s family Christian devotional. Recommended Reading Discerning Between Godly and Worldly Grief. I think we all sometimes have to try to determine whether a person is displaying godly grief or worldly grief. Sam Crites offers three marks to help us make that determination. Harvest in Fearful Times. Here’s Melissa Edgington on trusting the Lord with an uncertain future. “I’ve seen various types of hand-wringing over the past week about governments and militaries and potential power grid disruptions. I watched one video, and then social media began showing me a different side of the internet, where cowboy hat-wearing men hand out ‘top secret insider knowledge’ from the front seat of their pickup trucks. In fact, I saw individuals from all sides of the political spectrum worrying out loud about how much water they should have on hand, how many weeks’ worth of prescriptions, how many canned goods and what types of communication devices would be best.” Can I Love My Enemies While Addressing Wrongs and Protecting Myself? “Practically speaking, how then should we demonstrate godly love for our enemies—the kind of love that redeems and restores instead of perpetuating sin and injustice? Let’s consider three implications of godly love that help answer this question…” Jeremy Oliver offers counsel on a sensitive matter. Is Missions Too Costly for Kids? I think a lot of people wonder whether life on the mission field could cost their children too much. Jessica B. writes from experience. “Are my children also called to this? As a mama missionary, I wonder about our fitness for the task when our family of eight clogs airport security and labors in language study and ministry like a well-meaning circus. Will my kids catch a deadly virus from the airport carpet? Will beans be lunch every day? How can we possibly replace years spent with grandparents and a vibrant children’s church? Will they become healthy adults when this calling cuts not only us but them?” How AI Brought a Mathematician to Ecclesiastes. This is an especially interesting article from Alan Noble. “Nobody—not even the most informed futurist—knows the effect AI will have on careers in the future. Some predict we’ll mostly adapt and find new vocations. Some predict we’ll all be living lives of leisure in a hyper-abundant economy while robots do all the labor. But if I had to guess, I’d predict that some people are going to have at least some of their valuable labor replaced by AI in the near future. And when that happens, people will have a crisis of meaning.” Don’t Stock the Pantry With Temptation. Darryl Dash warns against stocking the pantry with temptation. “We are used to preparing for almost everything. We prepare our clothes, our food, our vacations, and more. Paul is saying that whatever you do, do not prepare to sin. Instead, actively take steps to cut temptation out of your life. Deliberately arrange your life so that sinful desires are harder to satisfy. Avoid certain environments. Put a filter on your phone. Cancel that streaming service. Throw away those books. Cut out influences that tempt you toward sin.” Headlines Here are just a couple of interesting headlines from Christian news outlets. Christianity Today reports that Churches Face a Shortage of Worship Leaders . “A growing shortage of worship leaders has researchers, educators, and pastors wondering if it’s time to rethink music ministry recruitment and preparation.” Maybe some churches will ask whether they actually need a worship leader, since I have often wondered whether it’s a necessity for many of them. Across the pond, Evangelical Times considers the government’s proposal to ban conversion therapy and says Secular Press Wakes Up to the Danger of Labour’s Plan to Criminalise Conve
